item2: The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and comes from the collection of the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is numbered and was added to the Corpus Gernsheim collection on January 11, 2006, through a donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Head of a Bearded Old Man (Godfather)" was made by Bernardino Lanino and is part of the collection of the Turin Biblioteca Reale. The work is a watercolor drawing on paper, executed with a brush in watercolor in gray-brown on greenish-blue paper. The dimensions of the work are 195 x 148 mm. 

The drawing was presented in the publication "Italian Drawings of the Biblioteca Reale di Torino" by A. Bertini from 1958 under catalog number 208. It is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Turin Royal Library is the Turin Royal Library.
The picture shows a man with a big beard.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and comes from the collection of the Corpus Gernsheim. It is identified as bh_gern_182512_post and was added to the g-sc on February 18, 2010, as a donation from the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta).

A sketchbook from the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia in Palermo, inventory number 5239, contains on leaf 5239/35 a drawing of a seated male nude. The drawing, which is probably of Sicilian origin, dates from the period between 1701 and 1800. 

The drawing was executed in chalk on buff-colored paper and measures 237 x 362 mm. It is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue and is listed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome under the number 31 A 23 51 (+1). The artist's signature is unknown.
The manager of the Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia manages the sketchbook with the inventory number 5239. The sketchbook is part of the collection and bears the inventory number 5239/35.
The picture shows a person sitting on the floor.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings is held by the Corpus Gernsheim. The photograph, identified as g-art 2006.06.12, was donated to the Corpus Gernsheim on June 12, 2006, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing is from the collection of drawings and prints of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage. It was created by Federico Barocci, also known as Federigo Fiori da Urbino, il Fiori, il Federico Barocci. The work is a study for his painting "The Descent from the Cross" in the Cathedral of Perugia. The drawing depicts the legs and feet of Christ and is executed in black chalk on blue paper. 

The sheet is 426 x 261 mm in size and is in a collector's passe-partout. It has brown spots in the lower third and a small defect at the top edge. The drawing was mentioned in the publication "Federico Barocci, Bologna 1985" by Emiliani.

The curator of the collection of drawings and prints 295-1844 KdZ is the Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation - State Museums in Berlin.
The picture shows legs with toes.

A photograph from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim collection, is shown here. The photograph is signed bh_gern_183184_post and dates from 2007. It was donated to the museum by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim as part of the Donazione Gernsheim. The photograph belongs to the category "g-art".

A sketchbook by Pietro Novelli (inv. 1565) is in the collection of the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo. It was created in 1565 and is numbered 30. The sketchbook is a work by the draftsman Pietro Novelli.

The drawing depicts the saints Christopher and Anthony of Padua. The drawing technique is pen and ink on ivory-colored paper. The dimensions of the work are 187 x 140 mm. The work is listed in the publication "Pietro Novelli e il suo ambiente, Palermo 1990" under number III.80.
The curator of the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo, Sicily, is in possession of a sketchbook (inv. 1565) dating from 1565.
The image depicts Saint Anthony of Padua and Saint Christopher.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is available online. The photograph, numbered  "post" and acquired as a donation from the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta) to the museum on April 22, 2004, is titled "post".

The drawing "Leda" is from the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement and is exhibited at Chatsworth House. The work was created by Leonardo da Vinci. The drawing is executed on paper in chalk and ink. The ink is brown, while the chalk is black. The pen is brown and was used in a wash technique. The drawing measures 160 x 137 mm. It is part of the Devonshire Collection and was described by M. Jaffé in his work "The Devonshire Collection...".
The Chatsworth House Estate is managed by the private collection trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement, numbered 717.

The picture depicts Jupiter in the guise of a swan, united with Leda, while from one of her eggs emerge the Dioscuri, the twins Castor and Pollux. At the same time, Helen, or Helen and Clytaemnestra, hatch from a second egg.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Gernsheim Archive. It comes from the collection of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and bears the catalog number 180538_post. The photograph was donated to the museum in 2005 and is designated g-art 2005.01.

The drawing "Design for a Glorifying Allegory for a High Ecclesiastical Figure" is by Domenico Maria Bonaveri and was produced in Munich by the State Graphic Collection. The work is a red chalk drawing with brown wash and measures 218 x 307 mm. It is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue.

The administrator of the State Graphic Collection in Munich is the city of Munich.

The State Graphic Collection Munich is a museum of graphic art.
The image depicts a portrait of a historical figure.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim, depicts a work of art. The photograph, numbered g-art, was taken on March 8, 2005, and was donated to the Corpus Gernsheim by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

Published by the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice, this work was produced by Vittorio Maria Bigari. The draughtsman was also Vittorio Maria Bigari. The work is titled "Two Cupids" and belongs to the genre of drawing. It is a black chalk drawing on grayish-brown paper. The dimensions of the sheet are 230 x 151 mm. The work is part of the Gernsheim catalogue and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager in Venice is the Fondazione Giorgio Cini.
The image depicts several small, amorous beings, known as putti or amoretti.

A photograph from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection, was donated in 2006 by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph is part of the "Corpus Gernsheim" collection and is designated bh_gern_181216_post.

The drawing "Atalanta and Hippomenes" was published in 1939 by the Munich State Graphic Collection. It is by Giovanni Antonio Pellegrini and was drawn by him. The drawing is a black chalk and pen drawing, lavished with chalk and pen. The dimensions of the drawing are 189 x 257 mm. It is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and can be found in the Gernsheim catalogue list under number 95 B (ATALANTE).  

The drawing is in the possession of the State Graphic Collection in Munich and was published there in 1939. It bears the number 21 and 11 in the Gernsheim catalogue.
The Munich State Graphic Collection acquired the object in 1939 under the inventory number 108. The object is in the care of the Munich administrator.
The image depicts a scene from Greek mythology, featuring the heroine Atalante.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings collection is held in the Gernsheim Corpus collection. The photograph is designated bh_gern_064542_post and was acquired on 7 November 2003 as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

The drawing "Justitia" was acquired by the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphische Sammlung, in 1872. Previously, it was in a private collection in Genoa. The last previous owner was Jacopo Durazzo. The drawing was created in 1554 by Giovanni Battista Paggi. 

The depiction is diagonally rectangular and drawn in brown on blue paper. It was executed in ink and with a pen and measures 256 x 182 mm. The drawing is documented in the catalog "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" by Ch. Thiem from 1977 (Cat. 40) and in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphische Sammlung, is the custodian of object 6238. The object was purchased in 1872. Prior to that, it was in a private collection in Genoa, which belonged to the Palazzo Durazzo until 1872 and was managed by Jacopo Durazzo.
The image depicts justice, personified as one of the four cardinal virtues.

The photograph depicts a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection. The drawing is part of the inventory number bh_gern_154739 and was donated to the museum on January 10, 2006, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The drawing is listed in the catalogue under the reference g-art 2006.01.10.

The drawing "Bishop before Saints Francis and Anthony and five kneeling believers" was made by Bernardino Lanino and is part of the collection of the Biblioteca Reale in Turin. The work is a watercolor drawing on ochre-colored, blue paper. The dimensions are 410 x 326 mm. The artist used a white-haired brush for the work.

The drawing was already mentioned in the publication "Italian Drawings from the Biblioteca Reale di Torino" by A. Bertini from 1958, catalog number 204. It is now located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Turin Royal Library is the Turin Administrator.
The image depicts a Roman Catholic archbishop or bishop showing Saint Francis and Saint Anthony of Padua. His hands are clasped, while a believer kneels before him.

The photograph comes from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of photographs documenting drawings. It is part of the Gernsheim Collection, a significant collection of artworks donated to the Art Museum in Bern. The photograph was donated to the Art Museum on March 8, 2005, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

The drawing "S. Giorgio Maggiore and Harbor" was made by Vittorio Maria Bigari and is in the possession of the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice. The gray wash drawing depicts the two buildings S. Giorgio Maggiore and the harbor. It measures 365 x 610 mm and has the number 25 I 1 46 C 23 23 1 in the Gernsheim Catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administration of the property in Venice is the responsibility of the Fondazione Giorgio Cini.
The image depicts a city view, a classic veduta, showing a gondola on the water.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Corpus Gernsheim. It is numbered and comes from the Gernsheim Collection. The photograph was donated to the museum on May 1, 2007, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph belongs to the category "g-art".

The drawing "Scene from the Life of Jesus: Healing of a Sick Person" was published by the art gallery manager of Bremen. It is by Leonaert Bramer, a 16th-century draftsman. The work is a drawing on paper, executed with a brush and gray-brown tone on white paper. The dimensions are 373 x 291 mm. The drawing is part of the Gernsheim catalogue, p. 1299, and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Bremen Kunsthalle in Bremen is the Bremen Kunsthalle Management Bremen 392.
The picture depicts the miracles of Jesus, particularly his healing power.
The photograph shows the Print Room in Berlin, which is part of the State Museum of Art and Cultural History Berlin (SMB). The photograph was taken in 2001 and shows the Print Room in a closed state.

Published by the Curator of the Prussian Cultural Heritage, State Museums Berlin, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints. The drawing dates from the Roman period between 1601 and 1700. It depicts male head and figure studies. The work was created by an anonymous artist and uses chalk and pen as drawing media. 

The drawing bears the signature 31 A 23 46 C 13 14 3. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the collection of drawings and prints is the Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room.
The image depicts people in various body positions, interacting with a donkey.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is shown here. The image is numbered bh_gern_068633_post and was donated to the museum on October 19, 2004. The donation was made by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "_ulans500006826_" by Giovan Gioseffo dal Sole was published by the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice. The work, executed in red chalk, dates from 185 x 231 mm in size and was created by Sole. The drawing is titled "_Giovan Gioseffo dal Sole_" and was made after a design by Guido, in a modern manner. The publication of the drawing was part of the "Drawing Art" series of Pelikan Drawing Art.

The drawing is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was documented by C. Thiem in the exhibition "Giovan Gioseffo dal Sole" in Bologna in 1990.
The administration of the property in Venice is the responsibility of the Fondazione Giorgio Cini.
The picture shows a pelican.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is shown. The photograph is numbered bh_gern_064367_post and was added to the collection on August 1, 2007. It comes from the collection of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and was donated to the museum.

The drawing "Diana the Huntress (Right Half)" is from the Flemish school and was created between 1601 and 1700, possibly also between 1701 and 1800. The work is in the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection, C 66/1445. It is a chalk drawing on light brown paper. The drawing is white and measures 525 x 753 mm. It is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue under number 94 Q 51 1 and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The State Gallery Stuttgart manages the Graphic Collection C 66/1445.
The picture shows Orion and Diana hunting.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of the Corpus Gernsheim. The image bears the internal number  and was donated to the Corpus on March 11, 2014, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The Corpus Gernsheim is renowned for its extensive collection of artworks and photographic documents from the history of photography.

The drawing "Figure Studies" was published in Album III/820 of the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The drawing, attributed to Vincenzo Chialli, was probably created between 1801 and 1840. 

The pen and ink drawing depicts figure studies and was executed in gray and ochre wash. It measures 380 x 265 mm and is currently located in the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Philadelphia Academy of Fine Arts, in Pennsylvania, is recorded in Album III/820.
The image depicts the nude human figure, representing the term "Corpo humano" according to Ripa.
A digital photograph from the Hamburger Kunsthalle depicts Christoph Irrgang's work "Locked". The photograph was taken in 2010 and is in color.

The drawing "Study for Perugino, Pietro Wall Painting The Adoration of the Shepherds" comes from the workshop of Perugino, more precisely from Pietro Vannucci, Pietro Perugino or Pietro di Cristoforo Vannucci. The sheet is a study for the wall painting "The Adoration of the Shepherds" and shows the kneeling Saint Joseph. The drawing was created with metalpoint on paper and is drawn in gray-brown and white. It measures 208 x 137 mm and is in the possession of the Hamburg Kunsthalle, Print Room. 

The drawing is part of the collection 73 B 2 11 H (JOSEPH) and was mentioned in the publication "Italian Drawings 1450-1800" by D. Klemm, catalogue number 383. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also possesses a copy of the drawing.
The curator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle, Print Room, is based in Hamburg.
The picture depicts the adoration of the Christ Child at the time of his birth. Joseph kneels before the Child.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings collection and is part of the Corpus Gernsheim collection. The image is numbered  and was donated on October 19, 2004, by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta). The photographs in the collection are classified as g-art.

The drawing "Standing Female Figure" was published by the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice. It was previously attributed to the artist Giovan Gioseffo dal Sole. In the catalogue raisonné C.: Giovan Gioseffo dal Sole, Bologna 1990, it was listed under "disegni non autografi". The drawing depicts a standing female figure and was executed in black and white pen. It measures 267 x 182 mm and is in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager in Venice is the Fondazione Giorgio Cini.
The image depicts a standing person representing the different stages of life.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is numbered and was donated on October 1, 2011 by the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photograph is classified as a work of art and has the inventory number g-art 2011.10.01.

The curator of the Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett in Copenhagen has published the work "The Canonization of Saint Ignatius of Loyola". The drawing is by Agostino Masucci and was also executed by him. The work is a chalk and pen drawing, lavished in black and brown. The dimensions are 240 x 149 mm. The signature reads "IGNATIUS" and the number 13 1 U. The work is listed in the catalogue "Roman Drawings before 1800" by U. V. Fischer-Pace, Copenhagen 2014, under number 113. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information.
The custodian of the object is the Kopenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett with the object number GB 5762. The object can be viewed on Tuesday, December 13th.
The image depicts Ignatius of Antioch.

The photograph depicts a work from the Photographicum of Drawings collection, the Gernsheim Collection. It bears the internal number bh_gern_070624_post and belongs to the category g-art. The photograph was added to the collection on February 3, 2005. The donation was made by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Two Seated Women in Antique Dress" was made by Pelagio Palagi and is dated between 1790 and 1860. The work, which is part of the collection of the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice, was created as a pen and ink drawing on paper with wash technique. The dimensions are 132 x 165 mm.

The drawing is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and bears the inventory number 31 AA 23 5 according to KHI Florence. Another inventory number may exist.
The administration of the property is the responsibility of the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice.
The image depicts a seated female human figure.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. It comes from the Gernsheim Archive, more precisely from the collection of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph was donated by the Gernsheims on January 13, 2005, and bears the inventory number g-art.

The drawing "Christ Blessing a Saint" comes from the Biblioteca Riccardiana in Florence and is attributed to Bernardino Barbatelli. It depicts a black chalk drawing on paper measuring 209 x 286 mm. The back of the drawing bears the signature "Bernardino Poccetti". The work was presented by M. Chiarini in the catalogue "The Drawings of the Biblioteca Riccardiana di Firenze" from 1999 and listed there under number 14. The drawing is now located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager is Florenz Biblioteca Riccardiana 270.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of the Gernsheim Museum. The image is cataloged under the number 7793 and is part of the Gernsheim Donation. It was donated in 2004 by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and is classified as g-art.

In 1848, the curator of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi, Andrea Meldolla, published a drawing. The work, a study of the human form, was executed by Andrea Schiavone. The drawing, in pen and ink on chamois-colored paper, measures 187 x 278 mm. It is part of the Gernsheim Collection and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Florence Uffizi Gallery is Florence. He took office in 1848.
The image depicts a nude human, representing the human form in all its aspects.

A digital photograph from the Hamburger Kunsthalle, provided by the bpk, is in.tif format and has the internal designation bhex-hamburger-kunsthalle-bpk-art 2010.01.28. The photograph is in color and is currently restricted.

The drawing "Perseus with the Head of Medusa" is by the artist Giulio Romano. The work, executed on paper with chalk and ink, is in the Print Room of the Hamburg Kunsthalle. The drawing depicts Perseus carrying the head of Medusa. The dimensions of the drawing are 327 x 161 mm. It is in black and brown and is mounted on laid paper. 

The drawing was listed by D. Klemm in the catalogue "Italian Drawings 1450-1800" under number 257.
The curator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Kunsthalle.
The image depicts Perseus fleeing with the severed head of Medusa.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim collection. The image is numbered and dates from 2006. It is a gift from the Gernsheim family, specifically Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph was donated to the Corpus Gernsheim on March 4, 2006.

The drawing "Minerva and the Muses on Mount Helicon (?)" was made by Battista Naldini. Giovanni Battista Naldini is listed as the draughtsman. The work is a chalk drawing on paper, washed with pen and black chalk. The drawing measures 317 x 235 mm and bears the inventory number 92 C 25 1. It is in the possession of the State Graphic Collection Munich and was listed in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the State Graphic Collection in Munich is the Verwalter München. 

The object number of the object is 2287.
The picture depicts Minerva visiting the Muses on Mount Helicon to see the Hippocrene spring, which Pegasus had recently created.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection that is part of the Corpus Gernsheim. The photograph dates from 2003 and is numbered . The image is part of the "g-art" collection, which came to the museum through a donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Study for a Seated Female Figure" is by Carlo Palucci. The work, produced by him, depicts a seated female figure. It is a red chalk drawing on paper measuring 167 x 123 mm. The drawing is in the possession of the Pinacoteca Civica in Ascoli Piceno. It was exhibited there in 1995 in the exhibition "Papetti, Ascoli Piceno, Pinacoteca Civica", catalogue number 124. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information on this work.

The administrator of the Pinacoteca Civica in Ascoli Piceno is the firm r.

The address of the administrator is Pinacoteca Civica 433/422.
The picture shows a seated figure.

The photograph shows the Corpus Photographicum, a collection of drawings. It originates from the Corpus Gernsheim, specifically from item number bh_gern_015487_post. The photograph was donated to the Kunstmuseum in 2004 as part of the Donazione Gernsheim, a gift from Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.  Permission for publication was granted by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Reading Boy" is part of the Royal Library in Windsor Castle and was created by Guercino. The work was created between 1601 and 1700 and depicts a young boy sitting at a table reading. The drawing is a preparatory sketch for a larger artwork and was created in chalk on blue-gray paper. It measures 277 x 205 mm. 

The drawing has been examined by various experts and described in scholarly publications such as "The Drawings of Guercino in the Collection of her Majesty the Queen at Windsor Castle" and "Bolognese drawings of the XVII and XVIII centuries in the Collection of her Majesty the Queen at Windsor Castle".
The administrator is Windsor, located at Windsor Castle Royal Library, RL RL 3486.
The picture shows a boy, between toddler and teenage years, sitting at a table. Another boy, also between toddler and teenage years, is also in the picture.

The photograph depicts the work "Corpus Photographicum of Drawings" from the Gernsheim Collection, with the number [removed]. The image was acquired on March 10, 2004, as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

A draft for a villa, a pen drawing by Andrea Palladio, was published in the 17th century as part of the publication "Palladio, Vol. XVII" by the London Royal Institute of British Architects. The drawing depicts the facade and floor plan of the villa and is part of the "Drawing Art" series within architectural drawing. The dimensions of the drawing are 414 x 263 mm and it is marked with the numbers 48 C 14 23 and 48 C 14 25. Further information can be found in the publication "L. Puppi, Andrea Palladio, Milan 1974, Vol. 2, Cat. 10" from the Gernsheim catalogue list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the property is the London-based Royal Institute of British Architects. This institute is renowned for its publication of the Palladio Collection, Volume XVII.
The image shows the floor plan of a building.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and belongs to the Gernsheim Collection. It is numbered bh_gern_069087_post and was acquired on May 12, 2004 as a gift from the Gernsheims, Walter and Jutta.

The drawing "Madonna with Child, Saint Anthony Abbot and Another Saint" is part of the collection of the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice. It was made by Gaspare Diziani. The work is an oval drawing in sepia crayon on yellow paper, mounted on cardboard. The dimensions are 212 x 173 mm. The pen drawing was washed with ink and executed in red sepia crayon.

The work was mentioned in a catalogue by T. Pignatti, "Ancient Drawings of the Museo Correr", Volume 2, Venice 1981, under number 381. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Venice Museo Correr and Quadreria Correr Collection of Drawings and Prints is 979.
The image depicts the Madonna with the Christ Child floating in the air, suspended on clouds.  Beside her stand Saints Anthony Abbot and other accompanying saints.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is shown here. The image, signed bh_gern_117809_post, dates from 2005 and is titled g-art. It was donated to the respective museum in 2005 by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

The drawing "Angel and Figure Studies for a 'Redemption of Penitent Souls from Purgatory'" was made in 1544 by Jacopo Palma (Palma il Giovane). It is a preparatory drawing for a painting and depicts angels and figures. The work is executed on paper in chalk, sanguine, ink, and pen. The colors are black and brown. The drawing measures 231 x 161 mm. It is located in the Galleria Estense di Modena and was first published in the publication "Drawings from the Galleria Estense di Modena" by J. Bentini (ed.) in 1989.
The manager of the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense is the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense 1161.
The image depicts the liberation of souls from purgatory by angels who carry a naked man into heaven.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection within the Gernsheim Archive. It is part of the Corpus Gernsheim collection and is numbered  gern_086284_post. The photograph was taken on November 3, 2005, and is part of the Donazione Gernsheim, a gift from Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. Permission for the use of the photograph has been granted.

The design for an altarpiece was created by Il Parmigianino around 1530 in Florence. The work has been in the possession of the Fogg Art Museum in Cambridge, Massachusetts, since 1932. Previously, it was part of a private collection in Florence belonging to Charles Loeser. 

The drawing is executed in brown ink on chamois-colored paper and shows a pen drawing of 126 x 94 mm. The design has already been presented in publications such as "Old Master Drawings" by K. Oberhuber from 1979 and the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the object is the Cambridge (Massachusetts) Fogg Art Museum, which has managed it since 1932. The object has the inventory number 1932.297. It was previously in a private collection in Florence belonging to Charles Loeser.
The image depicts an altarpiece depicting the Holy Family in a "Sacra Conversazione".
A photograph from the Kunstpalast Museum, number 174/8079-20, shows a work of art from 1995. The artwork is currently closed.

The drawing "Study for Passeri, Giuseppe - Design The Flagellation of Christ" is from the collection of the Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf. It was made by Giuseppe Passeri and is executed in red and white on blue-green paper with chalk on the back. The drawing measures 413 x 274 mm and bears the inventory number 73 D 35 1.

The drawing is part of the collection of the Curator Museum and was described in the publication "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" by Dieter Graf in 1995. The Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome also possesses a copy of the drawing.
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is the KA (FP) verso.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and is part of the Corpus Gernsheim collection. The image is numbered g-art and was donated on February 7, 2005, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph has been classified as a work of art.

The painting was published in the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf as part of the FP 4469 collection. It is a drawing by Guglielmo Cortese, produced by Guillaume Courtois and Guglielmo Borgognone. On the front of the double-sided sheet with the number T,001, there is a study for the mystical marriage of Saint Catherine. The drawing was made with red chalk on paper measuring 241 x 189 mm. The work is 11 HH in size and was described by D. Graf in his 1976 publication "The Drawings of Guglielmo Cortese and Giovanni Battista Gaulli" in Düsseldorf. It is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is FP 4469.
The image depicts a female saint, Catherine of Siena.

The photograph shows a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. The drawing is from the Gernsheim Corpus and has the internal number bh_gern_038903. It is a work of art from the Gernsheims' collection, which was announced in 2011. The donation was made by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Standing Couple, Seen from Behind" is part of the collection of drawings and prints in the Print Room of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage. It is attributed to Hendrick Goudt and was probably created in a traditional manner. The drawing depicts a standing couple from behind and was made with pen on paper measuring 142 x 95 mm.

The traditional attribution to Adam Elsheimer is discussed in the literature. J. The administrator of the Rom Bibliotheca Hertziana, Planarchiv, published designs by the architect Giuseppe Papillo. These designs were created as part of an architectural competition for the renovation of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in April 1995. The drawings, executed in various formats and perspectives, show detailed floor plans, sections, and views of the planned new building. They document the various floors of the building, from the 2nd basement to the 5th floor, including the terrace.

The drawings also include system plans, courtyard facades, sections, and views that illuminate the courtyard, the mask portal, and the transition to the Palazzo Stroganoff. In addition, there are drawings of the reading area and the entrance to the Palazzo Zuccari. The detailed drawings by Giuseppe Papillo offer a comprehensive insight into his vision for the renovation of the Bibliotheca Hertziana.

The published sketch sheets include floor plans, sections and elevations of each floor, including the ground floor, basement floors, and upper floors up to the fifth floor and the terrace.

Furthermore, the drawings document the courtyard, the mask portal, and the transition to the Palazzo Stroganoff. Further views show the reading area and system plans of the building. The drawings provide a comprehensive insight into Papillo's design and his vision for the modernization of the Bibliotheca Hertziana.

The Getty Research Institute in Los Angeles houses drawings by the architect Antonio Asprucci. The sheets come from the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and show preparatory drawings for various architectural projects. These include designs for fountains, fountain houses, a triumphal arch, and an urn with a base. Some drawings also show studies of an Egyptian fountain. Asprucci worked with pen and ink on paper.

The drawings are in various formats. "Designs for Fountains" and "Fountain House" are on 41 A 65 1 paper format, while "Design for a Triumphal Arch" and "Studies of an Egyptian Fountain" are on 43 A 42 2 paper format. "Urn with Base" was created on 42 E 34 paper format.
The administrator of this object is the Getty Research Institute Special Collections in Los Angeles.

The drawing, executed in ink, chalk, and pen on paper, shows a floor plan of the church. Antonio da Sangallo used brown and light brown ink, red chalk, and pale yellow and gray pen drawings.

The work is executed on heavy paper measuring 423 x 330 mm. The signature reads "48 C 14 23 : 11 Q 71 1 : 61 F (SAN PIETRO) 61 E (ROMA)". The scholarly edition "The architectural drawings of Antonio da Sangallo the Younger and his circle" by Ch. Frommel and N. Adams from 2000 lists the work. The Codex Mellon, also known as the "Menicantonio Sketchbook," is a remarkable architectural sketchbook attributed to the Italian artist Antonio da Domenico Chiarelli. Dating back to 1513, the codex contains a wealth of detailed drawings and sketches that offer valuable insights into the architectural styles and techniques of Rome during the High Renaissance.  

The sketchbook is filled with architectural studies, including detailed renderings of ancient Roman ruins, such as the Pantheon, the Colosseum, and Trajan's Forum. Chiarelli meticulously documented various architectural elements, such as columns, capitals, archways, and friezes. His drawings also encompass a range of architectural projects, from grand palaces and churches to smaller-scale structures. The codex provides a unique glimpse into the mind of a master artist and the artistic and architectural currents of his time.

The Mellon Codex is in the possession of the Pierpont Morgan Library in New York. The Department of Drawings and Prints (PML 1978.44 B3 027 08) is responsible for its administration. Previously, the codex was in a private collection in Washington before it came into the possession of Paul Mellon. It then went into a private collection in New York belonging to the art dealer Hans Peter Kraus. 

Before its acquisition by Paul Mellon, the codex was in a private collection in Bologna (Aimo, Domenico) and before that in a private collection in Rome (Fontana, Carlo).

The Codex Mellon, a sketch book by the Italian artist Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli, is a valuable resource for understanding architectural design in the Renaissance. The book contains numerous detailed drawings of ancient Roman structures, including temples, basilicas, and tombs, as well as architectural elements such as columns, capitals, and cornices. Chiarelli's meticulous renderings capture the intricate details of these buildings, showcasing his keen eye for proportion and perspective.

The Codex Mellon also features sketches of contemporary buildings and projects, including designs by renowned architects. These sketches provide insight into the evolving architectural styles of the time and the innovative ideas being explored by Renaissance masters. The book's diverse range of subjects, from ancient ruins to modern commissions, highlights Chiarelli's versatility as an artist and his important role in documenting the architectural heritage of Rome.

The Codex Mellon, also known as the "Menicantonio Sketchbook", is a sketchbook by the Italian artist Antonio da Domenico Chiarelli. It dates from 1513 and contains many architectural drawings, mainly focused on Roman antiquities. The sketchbook has 87 numbered pages and includes a variety of sketches, from detailed studies of individual architectural elements like capitals, bases, and cornices to complete reconstructions of structures like the Pantheon, the Colosseum, and the Baths of Caracalla.

Chiarelli's drawings show his thorough understanding of Roman architecture and his sharp eye for detail. He often added precise measurements and notes, showing his desire to record and analyze the buildings he observed. The Codex Mellon offers valuable information about the architectural scene in Rome in the early 16th century and is a tribute to the artistic and scholarly achievements of Antonio da Domenico Chiarelli.

The Codex Mellon is held by the Pierpont Morgan Library in New York, managed by the Department of Drawings and Prints. The catalog number is PML 1978.44 B3 027 08. It was previously part of a private collection in Washington belonging to the collector Paul Mellon. It then moved to a private collection in New York belonging to the art dealer Hans Peter Kraus. 

Before its time in New York, the Codex was part of a private collection in Bologna belonging to the collector Aimo Domenico. Prior to Bologna, it was in a private collection in Rome belonging to the collector Carlo Fontana.

The Codex Mellon, a sketchbook attributed to the Italian architect and draftsman Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli, is a rich collection of architectural designs. The codex, now located at the Pierpont Morgan Library in New York, contains many sketches and drawings of ancient Roman structures, including temples, basilicas, and triumphal arches. 

Chiarelli's precise drawings reveal a deep understanding of classical architecture and his sharp eye for detail. He illustrates both exterior and interior views of buildings, often using perspective and measuring tools to create realistic depictions. Among the notable structures depicted are the Pantheon, the Colosseum, Trajan's Forum, and the Baths of Caracalla. The Codex Mellon provides a valuable insight into the architectural practices and artistic tastes of the Renaissance period.

The collection consists of a series of architectural drawings by Giuseppe Barberi (1746), mainly depicting designs for the Palazzo Reale in Milan. The drawings illustrate various aspects of the palace, including facades, ground plans, sections, and studies for elements such as staircases, gardens, and interiors. 

Barberi's detailed and carefully executed sketches reveal his architectural vision and technical expertise. The drawings span from preliminary sketches to more finished renderings, providing insights into the development of the palace's design. The collection also features drawings for other buildings, such as villas, country houses, and a customs house, illustrating Barberi's wider architectural interests.

The curator of the private collection is Rome, though their exact identity is unknown. The curator is personally responsible for the management and care of the collection, and has extensive duties and responsibilities in this regard.

Published by the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Kupferstichkabinett, the drawing "Six Dancing Cupids with Garlands and a Palm Tree" is attributed to Giovanni Francesco Penni. The drawing was created by Giovanni Francesco Fattore, also known as "il Fattore". The work is part of the graphic arts and bears the inventory number ulan500021943.  

The drawing is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was entered in the collection catalogs with the identification letters 92 D 19 16 25 G 41 11.
The curator of the State Art Collections Dresden, the Print Room, is based in Dresden.
The image depicts putti carrying a wreath or garland.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, the Gernsheim Archive, is part of the art museum's collection. The photograph, numbered 160431_post, dates from 2006 and was donated to the collection by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The curator of the Fermo Biblioteca Comunale, Fortunato Duranti, published the Carducci inventory from 1439. The drawing was made by Fortunato Duranti and is in the Central Italian style. It is a work of the Zeichenkunst workshop and was created with ink and watercolor on white paper. The work is executed in black and white with a pen and measures 254 x 557 mm. The drawing can be found in the catalog "Catalogo mostra San Severino Marche, Milano 1984" under Kat. 77. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Fermo Biblioteca Comunale is the Fondo Carducci 1439 FC d. XVIII. 560.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim Collection. The image dates from 2006 and is designated bh_gern_142455_post. It is an artwork that was added to the collection in 2006 through the donation of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Female Allegory on Clouds with Coat of Arms and Angels" was made by Giovanni Baglione around 1570. The work, a black ink pen drawing, is washed with ink and chalk and depicts a female allegory on clouds, accompanied by a coat of arms and angels. The drawing measures 166 x 254 mm. The original is in the collection of the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Martin von Wagner Museum of the University of Würzburg is Mr. v. Wagner. The museum is located at the address 7157 v.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and originates from the Gernsheim Collection. The image is identified as bh_gern_182846_post and was donated on March 18, 2010, as part of the Gernsheim Donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

A sketchbook from the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia in Palermo was created between 1601 and 1700. The winged putto depicted in the drawing is a work of art. The drawing was made in red chalk on paper and measures 190 x 141 mm. The sketchbook was previously in the possession of the Abbazia di San Martino delle Scale in Palermo and the Museo Nazionale italiano in Palermo.

The first mention of the sketchbook is found in the Gernsheim catalogue, compiled by an anonymous author and kept in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The property manager is Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia. The sketchbook is registered under the inventory number /18. Former owners include the Abbazia di San Martino delle Scale and the Museo Nazionale, both in Palermo.
The image depicts several putti, portrayed as cupids and cherubs.
A photograph of the Kunstpalast from 1995 shows the state of the museum in September 1995. The photograph shows that the exhibition with the number 174/8365-5 was closed.

The drawing "Studies of Garments Over the Legs of a Seated Figure" is by Giuseppe Passeri. It is a preparatory drawing for a larger work and was drawn in chalk on blue paper. The back of the drawing is also covered in red and blue chalk. The dimensions of the drawing are 424 x 276 mm.

The drawing is in the possession of the Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf and was mentioned in the publication "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" by Dieter Graf. Another copy of the drawing is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is KA (FP) 9514 verso.

The photograph belongs to the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and originates from the Gernsheim Collection. It bears the internal number bh_gern_030407_post and was donated on April 20, 2005. The donation was made by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim, and both gave permission for publication. The photograph is classified as a work of art and is part of the g-art collection.

The work "Allegorical Triumphal Chariot" was published by the curator of the Rotterdam Museum Boymans-van Beuningen. It is by Filippino Lippi or his circle and depicts an allegorical triumphal chariot. The drawing was executed in pen and ink on paper and measures 115 x 139 mm. The work is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue under number 43 and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Rotterdam Museum Boymans-van Beuningen is the Rotterdam Museum administrator.
The image depicts an allegorical triumph, represented symbolically.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Corpus Gernsheim. It is numbered and was added to the Corpus on March 8, 2013, through a donation by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph's classification is g-art.

The drawing "Landscape with Temple" dates from 1919 and was created by Karl Friedrich Schinkel. The work is in the possession of the Hamburger Kunsthalle, Kupferstichkabinett, and bears the inventory number 1919.83 there. The work is a landscape with a temple, executed in drawing technique. Schinkel used chalk for the drawing, which may have been mixed with water or other colors. The dimensions of the drawing are 329 x 404 mm.  

The drawing is part of the Gernsheim catalogue list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Kunsthalle from Hamburg. It was founded in 1919. Object number 83 is part of the collection.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Corpus Gernsheim. It bears the identification number and was donated to the museum on December 31, 2011, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is currently restricted.

The design for a male figure in clothing with a walking stick is by Domenico Parodi and was published in 1777. The work is part of the "Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi" collection of the Florence Gabinetto. The drawing was executed in black chalk on squared paper and measures 209 x 130 mm. 

The drawing is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. The object number is 7177 S.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Collection. It was registered under the number  gern_067042_post. The photograph was added to the collection on May 2, 2009, as a gift from the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta Gernsheim). Publication approval was granted by the Gernsheim family.

The etching by the draughtsman Johann Georg Wille, titled "Sleeping Place in a Hut", was published in 1967 by the curator of the Print Room of the State Art Gallery Karlsruhe. The drawing, referred to as "b", depicts a sleeping place in a hut and measures 194 x 219 mm. It is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and is catalogued there under the number 41 A 76.
The curator of the State Art Gallery Karlsruhe, Print Room, was in Karlsruhe from 1967 to 1967.
The picture shows a bed.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection. The photograph is numbered and was donated on January 2, 2012, as part of the Gernsheim Donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph is cleared for use.

The etching "Head of an Old Man" was drawn by Leonardo da Vinci. The work is in the possession of the Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett in Copenhagen and is part of the Tu ital.mag.VII.52 collection. An alternative attribution is to Romano, Giulio. The drawing on chamois-colored paper was done with a pen and measures 108 x 74 mm. It is part of the Gernsheim catalogue list and the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom.
The administrator of the object is the Kopenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett. The object number is ital.mag.VII.52.
The picture shows a human head.
A photograph from 1998, taken by Réunion des Musées Nationaux, shows a work of art. The work of art's number is 3602, it is in black and white, and is currently closed.

The curator of the Paris Musée National du Louvre, Department of Graphic Arts, published a drawing. The drawing is Italian and dates from between 1501 and 1600. It is a copy after Aelst, Pieter van Edingen, and Raphael. The drawing is attributed to a carpet depicting the Adoration of the Shepherds. The drawing was executed in black and white ink on brown paper. The pen, ink, and brown paper are toned brown. The drawing measures 247 x 380 mm and bears the inventory number 73 B 25. 

It is located in the Musée du Louvre, Department of Graphic Arts, and is part of the Inventaire Général des Dessins Italiens V: Raphael, his workshop, his copists, Paris 1992, Cat. 1013. The Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome also holds documentation of the drawing.
The administrator of the Paris Musée National du Louvre, Department of Graphic Arts, is Paris Musée National du Louvre Department of Graphic Arts 3602.
The picture depicts the adoration of the Christ Child by shepherds. Mary and Joseph are also present.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and is designated bh_gern_118107_post. It is part of the Gernsheim Corpus and was added to the collection on January 28, 2005, through the donation of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The reclining male nude was drawn by Francesco Stringa. The work was created in 1893 and is a drawing on paper in sanguine. The dimensions are 385 x 513 mm.

The nude is part of the Galleria Estense di Modena and was documented in the publication "Disegni della Galleria Estense di Modena" by J. Bentini (ed.) from 1989. The Hertziana Library in Rome has further documentation of the work.
The manager of the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense is the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense 893.
The image depicts a person lying on their side, stretched out. The posture and gestures of the arms and hands relate to the head position.

The photograph belongs to the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and is part of the Corpus Gernsheim collection. It bears the catalog number and was donated on April 20, 2005, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. Publication approval was granted by the donors.

The photograph is classified in the "g-art" category and is considered a work of art.

The work "Judith Beheading Holofernes, Front View" was published by the Williamstown (Massachusetts) Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute. It is a drawing by Battista Naldini, executed by Battista Naldini and Giovanni Battista Naldini. The drawing is in black chalk and red chalk, measuring 239 x 170 mm. It is in the possession of the Gensheim Catalogue Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom.
The administrator of the object is the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown, Massachusetts. The object number is 18.13.
The picture depicts Judith and her maid putting Holofernes' head into a sack.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is marked with the number bh_gern_115727_post. The photograph was donated to the museum on April 21, 2006, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. It was assigned to the category "g-art".

The drawing "The Sermon of John the Baptist" is by Domenico Pedrini. It is part of a private collection and was published in an unknown location. The drawing is executed in laviert with pencil, sepia, and pen, and measures 288 x 210 mm. It is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue.

The drawing was made by Domenico Pedrini himself.
The object is in the possession of a private collector, whose location is unknown. The administrator is unknown.
The picture depicts John the Baptist preaching, possibly with Christ among the listeners.

The photograph "Corpus Photographicum of Drawings" is from the Gernsheim Collection. It has the inventory number _gern_151600_post and was donated to the museum on December 31, 2011, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph is currently restricted.

Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi, the curator, has produced drawing 7179 S. Domenico Parodi is the artist who drew the allegorical figure holding the papal insignia. The drawing was created in the field of drawing and executed in chalk and pen on paper. Its dimensions are 266 x 153 mm. The drawing is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi with object number 7179 S.

A photograph from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim, bears the number  gern_115726_post. The photograph was received as a gift from the Gernsheims, Walter and Jutta, on April 21, 2006. It is part of the g-art collection.

A work by the Spanish painter Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, from the circle of the draftsman Murillo, Estéban Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, is in a private collection. The drawing, titled "Guardian Angel," was created in the technique of pen and ink on chamois-colored paper and measures 260 x 206 mm.

The work is listed in the Gernsheim Catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, according to information. Further details about the curator and the precise location of the collection are unknown.

The object is in the care of a private collection, the location of which is unknown. 

The collection is private and consists of four objects.
The picture shows an angel protecting a child.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Gernsheim Collection. It bears the inventory number bh_gern_073263_post and was donated to the collection on January 2, 2012, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The Gernsheim family has granted permission for the use of the photograph.

The curator of the Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett in Copenhagen has published the work "Saint John". The drawing is by Giovanni Francesco Barbieri, known as Il Guercino. The artist, who is also known as Francesco Barbieri or Giovanni Francesco Il Guercino, created the work in red chalk on paper measuring 227 x 202 mm. It is suspected that Salvi, Giovanni Battista, also known as Sassoferrato, may have also made the work. An alternative attribution is to Simone Cantarini. The work is part of the Gernsheim Collection and is listed in the catalog of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the object is the Kopenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett. The object number is GB 7400. 

The object is located in ital.mag.VII.22.

A digital photograph is located in the Bibliothèque du Ministère de la Guerre. The photograph, numbered SHDBG_D_Gb25_0045_H.tif, is titled "bhex-vincennes-shdbg-d-gb25-0045-h". It was digitized on August 30, 2011, and is in color. Reproduction of the photograph is prohibited.
The administrator of the Vincennes Bibliothèque du Ministère de la Guerre is G.b.25.

The photograph belongs to the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and comes from the collection of the Corpus Gernsheim. It is designated bh_gern_083614_post and was accepted into the Corpus on May 17, 2011 as a gift from the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta). The photograph was classified as a work of art.

The drawing "Court Scene with Janus-faced Figure and Musicians" is by Bernard van Orley. It is in the Chatsworth House Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement Collection and belongs to the Duke of Devonshire. The drawing was made in Orley and is in black chalk on brown paper. 

Further details about the drawing are: brushwork in white and gold, the size is 369 x 467 mm, the inventory number is 41 AA 12 43 A (+3) and 43 A (+4) and it is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Chatsworth House Estate is managed by the Chatsworth House Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement Collection. The estate is overseen by the Duke of Devonshire.
The picture shows the interior of a bourgeois castle, decorated in a festive atmosphere with numerous celebrations.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of photographs of drawings. It is signed bh_gern_133090_post and labeled GERN_133090_post. The image is in black and white and was scanned on October 18, 2018. It was donated to the museum by the Donazione Gernsheim, from Jutta Gernsheim and Walter. The photograph is currently restricted.

Published by the State Museums of Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints, the drawing is part of the Overbeck Collection 85. It was made by Friedrich Overbeck and shows the front of a design for a wall painting. The wall painting depicts the scene "Gerusalemme liberata" from the work of Torquato Tasso. The design originates from the Villa Giustiniani (Casino Massimo) in Rome and is intended to be a fresco.

The drawing was executed in pencil, red chalk, and pen on paper and measures 412 x 587 mm. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the collection of drawings and prints SZ Overbeck 85 is the Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings depicts a drawing. The photograph, numbered bh_gern_069337_post, comes from the Corpus Gernsheim collection. It was donated to the Corpus Gernsheim on June 9, 2004, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The drawing is part of the g-art collection.

The drawing "The Courtyard of the Palazzo Van Axel" is by Francesco Guardi and was made in 1712. It is a sepia drawing on paper, measuring 173 x 129 mm. The drawing is in the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice and belongs to the "Raccolta Disegni e Stampe" collection. It is part of the museum's collection and was previously mentioned in the publication "Disegni Antichi del Museo Correr, Vol. 3" by T. Pignatti from 1983, catalogue number 647 v. The reverse side of the drawing was recorded by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Venice Museo Correr and Quadreria Correr Collection of Drawings and Prints is 911.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of the Gernsheim Archive. It comes from the collection of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and was donated to the archive on June 8, 2004. The photograph is designated bh_gern_069337_post and was classified as g-art in 2004.

The drawing "Fishermen and Boats" is by Francesco Guardi and was created in 1712. The work is in the collection of the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice and is part of the Raccolta Disegni e Stampe. The drawing was executed in ink on gray paper and shows a brown pen drawing. 

It is 228 x 317 mm in size and is mentioned in the catalog "Disegni Antichi del Museo Correr, Vol. 3" by T. Pignatti from 1983 under number 576. The drawing is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Venice Museo Correr and Quadreria Correr Collection of Drawings and Prints is 1191.
The picture shows a fisherman in a rowboat.

A photograph from the Klassik Stiftung Weimar depicts Louis Held. The photograph, taken on March 8, 2024, is in black and white and was created as part of an order from 1998. The full view of the photograph is restricted.

The drawing "Rocky, wooded landscape of central Italian type" was created by Johann August Nahl (the Younger). It depicts three female figures in the foreground, including a flute player, and is executed in watercolor on paper. The dimensions of the work are 597 x 818 mm. The work is signed and bears the signature "J. A. Nahl del." in the lower right corner on the mat. The Klassik Stiftung Weimar owns the work.
The Weimar Classic Foundation Weimar Graphic Collections is the custodian of object KK 257.
The picture shows a woman sitting in a forest with mountains in the background. She is playing a flute.

The photograph depicts a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is numbered 172324a and comes from the bh_gern collection. The image was donated in 2009 by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim through the Donazione Gernsheim. The image is classified as g-art and shows the upper part of the drawing.

The drawing "Conversion of Saul" is by Giacomo Ligozzi and is part of the Graphic Collections of the Klassik Stiftung Weimar. Formerly part of the Grand Ducal and State Collection, it bears the inventory number KK 8748. The paper sheet is washed with pen and brown ink and gilded. It is brown toned and measures 530 x 382 mm.

The drawing was described in the publication "Italian Drawings. Volume 1, Catalogue of the Collection. Former Grand Ducal and State Collection (Weimar)" by Ursula Verena Fischer Pace (Cologne/Weimar/Vienna 2008) under number 396. Further information can be found in the Gernsheim Catalogue List of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and in Stefan Morét's work.
The administrator of the Weimar Klassik Stiftung Weimar is the Graphic Collections, formerly the Grand Ducal and State Collection KK 8748.

A photograph of the Kunstpalast from 1995 shows the entrance area with the number 174/8786-5. The artwork, which was closed in 1995, has the inventory number 1995.09.

The painting is in the Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf, the curator's museum. It is a drawing by Giuseppe Passeri, executed on the front of the sheet. The drawing shows preparatory studies for a man bending forward with a cloth. The technique of the drawing is chalk on blue-green paper, the tones are in red and white. The dimensions of the sheet are 273 x 414 mm.

The drawing is mentioned in the catalogue "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" of the Düsseldorf Art Museum by Dieter Graf from 1995 under number 1030. The drawing is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is KA (FP).
The picture shows a person leaning forward and looking over a sheet of paper.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and belongs to the Gernsheim Collection. The image is designated bh_gern_020050_post and was acquired on June 12, 2006 as a gift from the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta).

Published by the Curator of the Berlin State Museums, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints. The drawing comes from collection 295-1844 KdZ. The draftsman is Federico Barocci, also known as Federigo Fiori da Urbino, il Fiori, il Federico Barocci. It is a study for Barocci's painting "Last Supper" in the Duomo of Urbino. The drawing shows a hand study of an apostle holding a knife. It has slight creases at the bottom and a small flaw at the top left. The drawing is firmly mounted on a collector's passe-partout. 

It is a preparatory drawing for the painting, executed in black and white chalk on brown paper. Red chalk was used for two hands. The dimensions of the drawing are 421 x 264 mm. The drawing is mentioned in the publication "Federico Barocci" by A. Emiliani from 1985, catalogue number 750. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the objects is the Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints. The object bears the number 295-1844 KdZ.
The image depicts a seated figure in a garment adorned with folds and shapes. The figure's hand is visible.

In the Kunstpalast, specifically in department 174, there is a photograph registered under number 9638-18. The photograph dates from 1995 and is currently restricted. It belongs to the Kunstpalast collection and was classified under number 18.

The work "Study for Passeri, Giuseppe Ceiling Decoration The Assumption of Mary around 1702" is from the Graphic Collection of the Kunstpalast Düsseldorf. It is a drawing by Giuseppe Passeri in which he prepared studies for the ceiling decoration of "The Assumption of Mary" in the Santa Maria in Campitelli in Rome, more precisely in the Cappella Altieri. The drawing is executed in red chalk on grayish-green paper with white parts and measures 432 x 284 mm.

The work is part of the Kunstpalast Düsseldorf collection and was already described in the publication "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" by Dieter Graf from 1995. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information on this work.
The curator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is KA (FP). This information is located on the back of the object.

The photograph depicts the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a work from the Corpus Gernsheim. The photograph was taken in 2005 and is designated bh_gern_177279_post. The image is classified as g-art and was donated in 2005 by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta). The Gernsheim family has released the image.

The Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum in Braunschweig owns a drawing by the artist Nicola Malinconico. The drawing, numbered Z. 157, depicts two seated female figures, possibly sibyls. The work is executed in gray wash with a pen and measures 152 x 208 mm. It is in the collection of the Hertziana Library in Rome.

The drawing is part of the Gernsheim catalogue and bears the catalogue numbers 31 B 6 (+82) and 31 A 23 5 as well as 31 B 6 (+72).

The administrator of the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum in Braunschweig is the Braunschweig Administrator.

The museum is listed under number Z. 157.
The image depicts a person with a striking facial expression that conveys both joy and surprise.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Collection. The image is numbered bh_gern_028249_post and was donated on March 1, 2011, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is currently restricted.

The drawing "Seated Woman with a Skull" is by Salvator Rosa and was published in the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. The work is a brown pen and ink drawing on paper. The dimensions are 130 x 101 mm and the signature reads "Rosa". The drawing is mentioned in the publication "The drawings of Salvator Rosa" by M. Mahoney from 1977 under Kat. 49.5. 

It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi is Florence.
The image depicts a skull, inscribed with handwriting.

A photo of Braun, Adolphe from 1912/1915, labeled "raro-art", is shown here. It is a charcoal print and was released by Braun, Adolphe. The photo is fully mounted and in good condition. On the back is a stamp with the inscription "K: Rs."

Published in the Royal Library of Windsor Castle, the work "Female Figure in Dress" by Giovanni Santi, created in 1435, is on display. The artist Giovanni Santi, who executed the white chalk drawing on paper measuring 248 x 180 mm, is also listed as the maker. The work is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and bears the inventory number 31 AA 23 1 48 A 98 52 there.
The curator of the Windsor Castle Royal Library is Windsor.
The picture shows a standing woman whose clothing is decorated with an ornament of fabric folds.

A photograph from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim, bears the number  gern_053073_post. The photograph was acquired by the museum on June 12, 2006 as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The classification of the photograph is g-art.

The drawing "Study for Barocci, Federico Altarpiece The Presentation of Mary in the Temple Chiesa Nuova Rome" is from the collection of drawings and prints of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage. It was created by Federico Barocci, also known as Federigo Fiori da Urbino, il Fiori, il Federico Barocci. The study shows shoulder and back studies of the shepherd for the altarpiece "The Presentation of Mary" in the Chiesa Nuova in Rome. The drawing is executed in charcoal on brown paper and worked out with black, light beige, and white chalk.

Partially, the drawing was squared with black chalk. It is on a collector's passe-partout and measures 270 x 409 mm. The drawing is mentioned in the literature, for example, in the publication "Federico Barocci" by A. Emiliani from 1985.

The administrator of the objects is the "Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints". The object with the number 295-1844 KdZ is located in this collection.
The picture shows a person with their shoulders and back visible, leaning forward.
A photograph of the Kunstpalast from 1995 shows the museum closed. The photograph is numbered 174/9638-1 and is part of the 1995.09 collection.

The painting "The Crucifixion of Christ" by Giuseppe Passeri, created around 1707/1710, is located in the Santa Salome in Veroli, 1st chapel on the right. The drawing presented here is a preparatory study for this work. It shows the front of a garment and was executed in white chalk on brown paper. The drawing is 422 x 280 mm in size and bears the signature "Passeri".

The drawing is in the collection of the Kunstmuseum Düsseldorf and was described by Dieter Graf in his work "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" (1995). It is part of the Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf collection and has also been documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The curator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is KA (FP). This can be seen on the front of the object.
The image depicts a person wearing a garment whose folds and movements are meticulously rendered.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, more precisely the image bh_gern_033523_post. It comes from the collection of the Corpus Gernsheim and was donated to the Institute on January 7, 2011, by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta).

The drawing "Christus am Ölberg und die drei schlafenden Jünger" is by Ercole de Roberti and was given to a private collection in Berlin in 1902 by Adolf von Beckerath. The sheet is vertically creased and has staple holes. It was created in brown ink on paper and measures 27.2 x 20.6 cm. On the reverse side is another drawing: "Writing Evangelist".

The first owner was Nicolaes Anthoni Flinck, who also kept the object in his private collection.

The pen drawings originate from the Hertziana Library in Rome and were acquired by Ernst Steinmann in 1933. The album, titled "Architectural Structures and Monuments in Avignon and the County of Venaissin: Pen Drawings by Pierre Mignard, 1640 - 1725" (title fictitious), contains a collection of drawings dedicated by Pierre Mignard to architecture and building. The drawings, executed in ink and pen on paper, depict a variety of buildings and monuments in Avignon and its surroundings. These include, among others, the Porta Visani, the Fons Oppidi Pontis-Sorgiae, the Obeliscus Avenionensis, the Porta Insulae, the Porta Exterior Ptochotrophii Insulani, the Ichnographia Portae Interioris Palatii Apostolici Avenionensis, the Ichnographia Munitionis Sancti Michaelis, and the Porta Balmarum.

The drawings are signed "P. Mignard Archit. Reg. Inven. Et delin." and date from the period between 1640 and 1725. They offer a valuable insight into the architecture and cityscape of 17th-century Avignon and the County of Venaissin.

Among the buildings depicted are houses in Arezzo, villas in Frassineto, Montecchio, Creti, Chinacce, Dolciano, Acquaviva, the Fattoria dell'Abbadia, the villa in Fojano, Bettole, Font'a Ronco, the Fattoria del Pozzo and the villa in Tegoleto. In addition, a warehouse in Ponte della Nave and the Fabbriche della Chiusa are depicted. Most of the drawings are 323 x 245 mm in size and bear the inventory numbers mta,T,001 to mta,T,017.
The administrator of the Florence National Central Library is Florence.

The map of the Val di Chiana was made by Niccolò Gamurini, an Italian draftsman and cartographer, in 1814. The collection includes several drawings, including views and floor plans of houses in Arezzo, country houses in various towns such as Frassineto, Montecchio, Creti, Chinacce, Dolciano and Acquaviva, as well as the Fattoria dell'Abbadia and the Fattoria del Pozzo. The drawings also depict country houses in Fojano, Bettole, Font'a Ronco and Tegoleto. 

Other works include a warehouse in Ponte della Nave with floor plan and views, as well as the Fabbriche della Chiusa. The drawings, executed in watercolor and pen and ink, are part of the collection of the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale in Florence and are from Gamurini's workshop.

The manuscript, produced by Johannes and Giovanni Grevembroch in 1760, is located in the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice and contains watercolor drawings of lavabos and other architectural details in Venetian buildings. The drawings, kept in the museum's Gradenigo Library, are accompanied by detailed captions that provide information about the location and context of the depicted objects.

The manuscript is bound in an elaborate cover adorned with the Gradenigo family crest and a Museo Correr bookplate. The drawings depict lavabos in various buildings, including the Palazzo Ducale, the Church of Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, and the San Michele in Isola monastery. The depicted objects also include a fireplace in the Palazzo Ducale with the coat of arms of Doge Agostino Barbarigo and a two-tiered fountain in the Church of Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari.

The manuscript, kept in the Museo Correr and the Quadreria Correr in Venice, dates from 1760 and was produced by Johannes and Giovanni Grevembroch. It contains watercolors and drawings dealing with the art of drawing and book arts. The book is adorned with a cover leaf with the coat of arms of the Gradenigo family and bears the book stamp of the Museo Correr on the cover. 

The manuscript contains 41 drawings, which mainly depict Venetian washbasins, fireplaces, and fountains. The drawings are detailed and often show the coats of arms and inscriptions of the respective buildings and families. Some drawings are inscribed with descriptions giving the name of the artist, the building, and the year of creation. The manuscript is a valuable source for the study of Venetian architecture and art in the 18th century.
The administrator of the Venice Museo Correr and Quadreria Correr is the Biblioteca Ms. Gradenigo Dolfin 229.

It contains drawings of washbasins, fireplace surrounds, and other architectural elements from Venetian buildings. 

The drawings are detailed and show various buildings from different eras, including the Palazzo Ducale, the Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, and the Church of San Sebastiano. The captions often give the name of the building, the artist, or the Doge who resided in the building. Some drawings are accompanied by additional texts that provide information about the history or significance of the objects depicted. A notable feature of the book is the dedication on the title page, addressed to Pietro Gradenigo and his associates.

The drawings, watercolored on book pages, depict details of buildings and facilities in various parts of the city, including palaces, churches, and monasteries.

Some of the depicted washbasins are adorned with coats of arms and inscriptions that indicate their owners or the year of construction. The drawings are detailed and showcase the artful execution of Venetian architecture and decoration. The manuscript is a valuable testament to the art and culture of Venice in the 18th century.

The Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale Palatino holds a collection of drawings by the renowned Florentine artist and architect Francesco di Giorgio Martini. These drawings, mainly executed on parchment with ink and occasionally with metalpoint, date from 1450 to 1500 and offer valuable insights into Martini's innovative designs for civil and military engineering. The subjects range from fountains and fortifications to machines for lifting weights and transporting materials. 

Notable among these drawings are depictions of waterwheels, cranes, and other ingenious devices for harnessing mechanical power. Martini's meticulous attention to detail and his understanding of both artistic and technical principles are evident in each drawing. His work reflects the intellectual and technological advancements of the Italian Renaissance, showcasing Martini's significant contributions to the development of engineering and architecture during this period.
The administrator of the object is Florenz Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale Palatino 767.

The collection consists of drawings and paintings, mainly portraits, scenes from Roman life, and caricatures.  The works are attributed to various artists, including Eduard Hübner, Karl-Joseph Begas, Robert Cauer, and Hermann Clementz. Several pieces are linked to the Deutsche Künstler-Vereinigung in Rome, suggesting a connection to the artistic community of that era.

Notable works include a charcoal drawing of a seated figure by Hermann Clementz, a watercolor portrait of L.B. Dawison by the monogramist HMD, and a painting of five artists riding donkeys through the Campagna by Carl Constantin Heinrich Steffeck. The collection provides a window into the artistic practices and social life of artists in Rome in the late 19th century.
