Permission for publication was granted on November 16, 2017.

The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Corsini published the painting. The still life with apples and flowers was painted by Pietro Paolo Bonzi. The artist was also known as Bonci, Pietro Paolo, Boncus, Pietro Paolo, Bongi, Pietro Paolo, Bonsi, Pietro Paolo, Cobbo dalle frutta, il Cobbo dei frutti, il Gobbo da Cortona, il Gobbo da' Frutti, Gobbo dei Carraci, il Gobbo, Pietro Paolo, Sellari, Pier Paolo or Pietro Paolo Bonzi. The painting is an oil painting on canvas measuring 36 x 47.5 cm. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Corsini 12 Depot.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the image number bhim00034793.tif, was taken on November 27, 2017. The photograph depicts the work HER8328a, a piece by Enrico Fontolan. The photograph was taken as part of the photo campaign 23/2017 from August 1 to 7, 2017. The photograph is in color, unframed, and released for use.

David with the Head of Goliath is a painting displayed in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Corsini in Rome. The portrait was created by an unknown artist between 1551 and 1650. The oil painting on canvas measures 227 x 146 cm. The Hertziana Library in Rome is responsible for cataloging the artwork.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome is located in the Palazzo Corsini. The institution is part of the Accademia dei Lincei.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the image number bhim00041011. The photograph, labeled "art," was taken on September 26, 2019, and is in color. It depicts a work by Enrico Fontolan from the photo campaign 25/2019. The image is a full view of the work with its frame.  Release for publication was granted on September 26, 2019.

The Four Elements, a series of lunettes, was painted by Stefano Pozzi. The works were bequeathed to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome in 1999. The previous owner was Fabrizio Lemme, who passed them on to his daughter Fiammetta Lemme. The series consists of four paintings: "The Element Air", "The Element Fire", "The Element Earth", and "The Element Water". Each painting is an oil painting on canvas and measures 31 x 60 cm. 

The works are now in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. They are part of the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (2008).

The custodian of the objects is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini. Objects 4584, 4585, 4586, and 4587 were donated in 1999. Previously, they belonged to Lemme Fabrizio in Rome.

The former owner was Lemme Luly, Fiammetta.
A photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana shows artworks created after 1995. The photograph is in black and white and has been released.

The painting "Herzogin Anna Amalia of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach and Traveling Companions in the Park of the Villa d'Este in Tivoli" was painted in 1789 by Johann Georg Schütz. The work, an oil watercolor on paper, depicts the Duchess and her friends at the Villa d'Este in Tivoli. The painting is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was previously in a private collection in Rome, owned by Karl Glingler.  

The work is a variant of a motif by Schütz and was painted in May 1789 in the "Rotonda dei Cipressi" to hear Goethe's Tasso. The painting was described in the catalog of the exhibition "Anna Amalia, Carl August and the Rise of Classicism 1757 - 1807" at the Weimar Palace Museum in 2007.

The administrator of the object is the Rom Bibliotheca Hertziana Kunstbesitz, with the object number C10103. The former owner of the object was the private Mond collection in Rome, which owned the object from 1895/1896. 

Previous owners were the private Glingler collection, Karl in Rome.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the number bhim00049120.tif, was taken on April 15, 2022. The photograph shows the back of an artwork, with the inventory number P0006743_inv_2219v. It is in color and is by Enrico Fontolan, who took the photograph as part of the photo campaign 37/2021. Release for publication of the full image of the back was granted in September 2021.

The Evangelist Matthew with the Angel was created by Guercino, the painter Giovanni Francesco Barbieri, around 1620. The painting is located in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 110 x 141 cm. In the lower left corner, the work bears the inscription "F.9". The painting depicts the Evangelist Matthew being addressed by an angel.  

The painting is part of a pair, to which a pendant by Guercino titled "The Evangelist Luke Shows the Sketch of the Madonna" belongs. This pendant is also located in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome.
The administrator of the property is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. The property is located in the Palazzo Barberini and the postal code is 2219.

The scan is by Roberto Sigismondi and is numbered 271.13. It is a picture of the "Trittico di Acqui" in the Cathedral of Acqui Terme in the province of Alessandria. The scan was made on January 21, 2009. The image is in color and dates from 1988. Roberto Sigismondi has released the image of the Presentation in the Temple.

The Triptych of the Madonna of Montserrat, also known as the Trittico di Acqui, is a painting by the Spanish painter Bartolomé Bermejo. It was created in Acqui Terme and is now in the Hertziana Library in Rome. The triptych is oil on panel and measures 11 F 42 2 73 A 31 1 73 B 41 11 H (FRANCIS) 11 H ( ) 11 (+5).
A photograph from the Getty Research Institute shows a panoramic view of a secured facility from the 1970s. The photograph is by Max Hutzel and is in black and white.

The painting "Mass at Bolsena" by Antonio Maria da Panico is located in the Farnese Church of San Salvatore. It was created between 1596 and 1603 and is an oil painting on canvas. The dimensions of the painting are 332 x 192 cm. 

Erich Schleier analyzed the work in his article "Panico, Gentileschi, and Lanfranco at San Salvatore in Farnese", which was published in the Art Bulletin.

A digital photograph of the Museo Amedeo Lia, taken on February 10, 2009. The photograph is numbered 34-334 and is part of the collection "bhex-la-spezia-museo-amedeo-lia-34-334". The photograph is in color and is currently restricted.

The triptych "Madonna dell'Umiltà with Saints John the Baptist and Christopher" was published by the curator of the Museo Civico Amedeo Lia in La Spezia. It is attributed to the painter Giusto di Giovanni de' Menabuoi. The painting is in Florentine or Paduan manner. The tempera on wood panel measures 54 x 51.5 cm.

The work is part of the museum's inventory and was first presented in the 1997 publication "Dipinti" by F. Zeri and A. De Marchi. Further relevant information is held by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the La Spezia Museo Civico Amedeo Lia is the firm 334.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the number bhim00033943, depicts a work of art. The photograph was taken on October 24, 2017, and is in color. It shows the work by Enrico Fontolan and is from the photo campaign 23/2017. The photograph was taken with a frame and released.

The painting "Landscape with Women at a Spring" was created by the painter Jan Frans van Bloemen, also known as Vanblommen or Gian Francesco Van Bloemmen. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 98 x 141 cm. The work is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Corsini in Rome. The collection is managed by the "Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica". 

The painting was exhibited in the Anticamera, North Wall. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the work.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Corsini is the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. The Anticamera, North Wall is located in the Palazzo Corsini.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, designated P0022031_CC.tif, has been created. The photograph was taken on February 13, 2025, and shows a full view of a work of art without a frame. The artist of the artwork is Enrico Fontolan. The photograph was released on September 9, 2024. It was taken in color and includes a Color Checker.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome received the painting in 1989 as a gift. The previous owner is unknown. The work was previously found in a private collection of De Chirico, Isabella Pakszwer. The painting is a variant of "Gioia ed enigmi di un'ora strana" from 1913. It depicts an Italian square with a statue (Piazza d'Italia con statua). 

It is an oil painting on canvas. The dimensions of the painting are 50 x 40 cm. The work bears the signature "G. de Chirico 1937" in the lower right corner. The dating of the painting is 1937/1976. The painting was mentioned in the publication "Giorgio De Chirico nelle collezioni della Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. 78 opere dal 1909 al 1975" by L. Collarile (ed.) in 1994.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome is the administrator of the 1989 bequest. The previous owner is unknown. The work was previously in a private collection belonging to the artist Isabella Pakszwer Far.

This is an unidentified photograph, likely from 1958. It is an albumen print, released as a gift by Werner Hoppenstedt. The photograph is mounted on the edge and is in good condition. On the back is a stamp with the K: Rs. stamp.

The painting "Thomas Killigrew and (?) William, Lord Crofts" by Anton van Dyck was created in 1638 and is part of the Royal Collection in Windsor Castle. The oil painting on canvas measures 132.7 x 143.5 cm and is in the collection under the number 61 B 2. The artist's signature reads "A. van Dyck." and the painting is dated 1638. 

An illustration of the painting can be found in the publication "Brown, van Dyck, 1982" on page 213, illustration 222. A photograph is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of Windsor Castle is Windsor. The Royal Collection manages Windsor Castle.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00045076.tif and bhim00045076, was taken on January 26, 2021. It is a color photograph by Enrico Fontolan from the photo campaign 38/2020. The photograph shows the back of an object, which has been released, and is identified as P0004350v.tif. 

Enrico Fontolan created the photograph on November 3, 2020.

The holy Hieronymus was painted by an unknown artist around 1601/1700 on a wooden panel. The oil painting is 50 x 35.5 cm in size and was donated to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in 1892 from the Torlonia collection. It was previously attributed to the Venetian painter Jacopo Palma, but is currently attributed to an unknown artist. The work is part of the F.N. 473 collection. 

It was mentioned in the publication "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Voudret (2008) on page 39. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds a copy of the work.
The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini is the Donazione Torlonia from 1892. The donation was made in 1892 and was numbered 915 F.N. 473.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the number bhim00045070.tif, was taken on January 26, 2021, under the number P0004345.tif. The photograph shows the full view of an artwork by Enrico Fontolan, taken as part of the photo campaign 38/2020. The image is in color and shows the work without a frame. Permission for publication was granted on November 3, 2020.

The design for an altarpiece of Blessed Bernardo Tolomei among the plague-stricken is by the painter Stefano Pozzi. The painting, executed as an oil painting on canvas, measures 74 x 61 cm.

The work was published by the administrator of the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini and is mentioned in the catalog "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Voudret (2008). Bernardo Tolomei was beatified in 2009.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome is located in the Palazzo Barberini, specifically at number 3586, in file F.N. 936.
A 1978 photograph of the Szépmüvészeti Múzeum shows artworks that were closed off at the time of the photograph.

The curator of the Budapest Museum of Fine Arts has released the painting "Joseph and Potiphar's Wife". The painting is by Francesco Providoni and was created between 1685 and 1696. It is an oil painting on canvas. The dimensions of the painting are 41 x 48.5 cm.

The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns another version of the painting.
The administrator of the property is the Budapest Museum of Fine Arts with the number 9788.

A digital photograph by Mario Polesel, taken with flash, depicts the subject "San Domenico, Chioggia". The photograph, with the file extension ".tif", is named "bhex-polesel-san-domenico-chioggia-757" and was taken on October 6, 2009. The photograph is in color and is by Rodolfo Polesel. The subject shows a close-up view of the upper zone, which is closed off.

The panel painting "Christ's Night Prayer in the Garden of Gethsemane" was made by Luigi Benfatto and Alvise Dal Friso. The painting was created in Chioggia and is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The dimensions of the painting are 73 D x 31 x 21.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00044991.tif, depicts the back of a work of art. The photograph was taken on January 11, 2021, and bears the number P0004222v.tif. It is in color and originates from the 37/2020 photo campaign by Enrico Fontolan, who released the photograph on October 30, 2020. 

The image shows a full view of the back of the artwork.

The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini published a painting in 1601/1700 depicting an angel appearing to Saint Roch in prison. The oil painting on wood measures 32 x 45 cm. The signature is unclear and could read ROCHO. DE / [..] JOAN [..]E. POLE [..].

The saint holds a cartridge in his hand, described by L. Mochi Onori and R. Voudret in the publication "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" from 2008. According to the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, the work is anonymous.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome is the Palazzo Barberini. The address is 3596 F.N. 946.

A digital photograph of Michelangelo, Mauro di, designated M33_07.tif, was archived on October 22, 2022, under the designation bhex-2022-30-220. The photograph was color-corrected on October 18, 2023.

The photograph was ordered in 2022 under number 30/2022. The rights to the photograph are divided, and the overall view is released.

The painting is located in the Madonna della Sbarra church in Panicale (Perugia). It is situated on the fourth altar to the left of the entrance. The altar is Umbrian and dates from the period between 1601 and 1700. The altarpiece depicts the Madonna with angels and saints. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 25 I1 11 H. 

Saint Francis and Catherine of Siena are recognizable in the painting. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about this work.

A photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana was taken by Enrico Fontolan on November 11, 2020, as part of the photo campaign 45/2020. The photograph is designated bhim00045506.tif and depicts the reverse side of the object art 2022.03.16 P0004778v.tif. The photograph is in color and has been released.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini, Rome, published the Torlonia donation 1140 F.N. 455 from 1892. The painting "Mary with Child and Angels" is a panel painting, created around 1627/1648. It was made by Simone Cantarini, a painter from Pesaro. The oil painting on wood measures 16 x 13 cm.

The work is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome and was described by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in their catalogue "Galleria Nazionale: Palazzo Barberini. I dipinti - catalogo sistematico" from 2008.
The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini is the Donazione Torlonia. The donation was given to the Palazzo Barberini in 1892. The donation is numbered F.N. 455.

A photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the image number bhim00019685, depicting the artwork "art 2015.03.24". The photograph was taken in color on March 24, 2015. Enrico Fontolan released the image on December 12, 2014.

The painting "Viola Guache" is from the private collection of Gabriella Palpacelli-Riccio and was created in 1981 by Lorenzo Guerrini. It is a panel painting in the format 50 x 70, executed in tempera and gouache on paper. The work bears the signature "L. Guerrini 81". Alessandro Brodini and Margherita Fratarcangeli dedicated an entry to the painting in their publication "Il segno astratto. La collezione Palpacelli da Avenali a Scialoja" from 2015 (Cat. C.12.1).
The curator of the collection is Marino, who also manages Gabriella Palpacelli-Riccio's private collection. The collection is called "Collezione Palpacelli-Riccio" and is cared for by Marino.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, titled "bhim00037227" and "HER0465.tif", was taken on November 7, 2018. The photograph is in color and shows a work of art by Enrico Fontolan from the photo campaign 25/2018. It is a full view with frame, which has been released.

The painting "Encounter," by the French painter Nicolas Lancret, is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The oil painting on copper depicts a scene measuring 27 x 35 cm and was documented by Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" from 2008.

The painting's catalog number is 33 A 13 1 41 A 22 3 33 C 23 21 and it is kept in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is Palazzo Barberini 2467.

This photograph, from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, depicts a rare artwork from 1912/1915. It is a large-format albumen print (38 x 28.2 cm). The photograph was taken in Rome, Italy, and is part of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica collection. The painting depicted in the photograph has been released by the artist. The photograph is fully mounted and bears a handwritten inscription "K.: Vs. hs." and a stamp on the back.

The "Maria Magdalena" is a panel painting from the Italian Renaissance. It was created around 1468 by Piero di Cosimo and is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome. The painting, which is 72 x 53 cm in size, depicts the Holy Mary Magdalene as a young woman with long, flowing hair. The original attribution to Andrea Mantegna was later corrected, and Piero di Cosimo was recognized as the true artist. 

The work is part of the Palazzo Barberini collection and was documented in Mochis "Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini i dipinti catalogo sistematico" (Rome 2008).

The custodian of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini is F.N.

Field: OBJ @ Title
Text: Santa Maria Maddalena

The title of the object is "Santa Maria Maddalena".
The photograph shows Gherardi from 1973 in black and white. It is a gift from Dall'Ora, possibly from Countess Dall'Ora. The photograph is restricted.

A portrait of an old man with a beard and a quill pen, created around 1972 by Franz von Lenbach, is in the private collection of the Dall'Ora family. The painting, originally part of the estate's collection, was sold to the Dall'Ora family in 1972. It is an oil painting measuring 100 x 76 cm and is titled "Portrait of an Old Man". The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome documented the work on January 17, 2019.
The object manager is the Dall'Ora family. They have been the private collection managers since 1972.

A rare photograph, originating from an albumen print in 1960, depicts an unknown person. The photograph was released and affixed to the edge. It is in good condition. The front is inscribed with ballpoint pen and pencil. The back features a stamp.

A portrait of a bearded man, painted by Christoph Amberger, is in the Musée d'Art Ancien in Brussels. The painting is incompletely recorded and unidentified. Its creation is believed to have taken place in Zurich. The artwork is currently in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the Brussels Musée d'Art Ancien could not be identified. 
In Zurich, however, an administrator was found.

A photograph at the Central Collection Point Munich, with the number CP144918, may depict a rarity from the "raro-art" collection of 2024. The print is a black and white silver gelatin photograph from the estate of the photographer Johannes Felbermeyer, who was admitted to the collection in 1997. The photograph is labeled with a handwritten label that mentions Leonardo da Vinci's "Leda" and the restitution from Italy with the designation CCP Mü-Nr. 1738.

The photograph shows a print measuring 16.4 x 10 cm and is an overall view that has been released.

The curator of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi has published the painting "Leda and the Swan". The work was created by Leonardo da Vinci. It was previously attributed to Leonardo da Vinci. The painting dates from around 1505/1515.

It is an oil painting on wood, measuring 131 x 78 cm. Frank Zöllner describes the painting in his work "Leonardo da Vinci 1452 - 1519, The complete paintings" published in 2011.

The manager of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi is Florence. 

The gallery has the object number 9953r.

A photograph of Perugia from the Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria dates from between 1940 and 1944. It is an albumen print, fully adhered and heavily faded and stained. On the back is a Fox stamp. 

Two photographs are glued together, as documented by the notation "K: zwei Ks. aufeinandergeklebt".

The painter Domenico di Paride Alfani created the painting "Holy Family with Saints Anna, Joachim, and the Infant John". The work, a panel painting on wood, was painted with oil and measures 73 B x 82 H. It is located in the Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria in Perugia and was published by the curator. 

Another copy of the painting is held by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, marked "cfi".
The administrator of the Perugia Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria is the Perugia administrator.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from 1940/1944 is found in an albumen print from 1895. The photograph is fully adhered and yellowed, showing adhesive stains, fingerprints, and foxing. Two cardboard mounts are glued together and bear the stamps of Fox.

The dead Christ with Mary and Saints, a panel painting, was created by Cima da Conegliano, also known as Giovanni Battista Cima, Giovanni Battista Cima da Conegliano Coneglianensis, Joannes Baptista Cima or Giambattista Giovanni Battista da Conegliano. The work was created between 1517 and 1518 and measures 73 cm in height and 115 cm in width. In the lower center of the panel is the inscription "IOANNIS BAPTISTE CONEGLANENSIS OPUS", which also serves as the artist's signature.

The painting is in the possession of the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice and was mentioned by Moschini Marconi in his catalog number 112 in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome in 1955.
The manager of the Venice Gallery dell'Accademia is "Venice Manager".
A black and white photograph from 1976 shows a full view of the BAS NA Camp. The photograph is restricted.

The administrator of the Caserta Royal Palace commissioned the painting "God the Father" between 1601 and 1700. The painting is an oil painting on panel and measures 11 centimeters high and 23 centimeters wide (+3 cm). The work is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Caserta Royal Palace is Caserta.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the capture ID bhim00037144.tif, was taken on October 25, 2018 under the designation HER0313a.tif. The photograph shows a color image by Enrico Fontolan from the photo campaign 25/2018. It is a full view of a work of art without a frame. The photograph has been released.

The painting "Allegory of Europe" is by Francesco Trevisani, a painter from Rome. It was painted in the Palazzo Castelbarco Albani in Urbino and is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome. The work is an oil painting on canvas measuring 74 x 57.5 cm. 

The first edition of the work was published in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" edited by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in Rome in 2008. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has a copy of the painting.

The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. 
The address of the Palazzo Barberini is 2550.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as "bhim00037143.tif" and "HER0313.tif", was taken on October 25, 2018. The photograph depicts a work of art, classified as "art", and was captured during a photo campaign in August 2018. It is a full view of the artwork, including the frame, which has been released. The photograph was taken by Enrico Fontolan.

The painting "Allegory of Europe" by Francesco Trevisani originates from the workshop of the Roman painter Francesco Trevisani. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 74 x 57.5 cm. The work is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome.

It was previously part of the collection of the Palazzo Castelbarco Albani in Urbino. The Palazzo was managed by the Albani family from Rome. The painting was first exhibited at the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome, which is located in the Palazzo Barberini.

The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is located in the Palazzo Barberini.

The address is Palazzo Barberini 2550.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00037161.tif and bhim00037161, was taken on October 29, 2018. The photograph depicts a work of art by Enrico Fontolan from the HER0354_scont.tif collection. The photo shoot took place in August 2018 as part of the 25/2018 project. The photograph is in color and shows a full view of the artwork with a detached frame.

The portrait of Cardinal Vincenzo Maria Altieri was published in 1989 by the administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini. The painting was executed by Anton von Maron and depicts Vincenzo Maria Altieri in an oval painting on canvas in a rectangular format. The oil painting measures 162 x 114 cm.
The administrator of the Rome National Gallery of Ancient Art is located in the Palazzo Barberini.

A photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana depicts a rare artwork from the years 1922 to 1933. The photograph was made as a large-format albumen print measuring 38.2 x 27.2 cm in 1953 or 1956.  

The photograph is fully released and inscribed on the back with K.: Vs. Rs. hs. and a stamp.

The painting "Young Woman" by Domenico Ghirlandaio is in the possession of the Galleria degli Uffizi in Florence. It was added to the Pinacoteca collection in 1892 and bears the inventory number 1892, 8380 there. The work was created in the workshop of Domenico Ghirlandaio and was executed with the assistance of Domenico Bigordi and Domenico Grillandajo. The oil painting depicts a young woman and measures 65 x 48 cm.
The administrator of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi Pinacoteca is the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi Pinacoteca. The inventory number is INV 1892, 8380.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the capture ID bhim00038786.tif. The photograph, taken on April 24, 2019, is part of the photo campaign 117/2019 and shows a full view of a work of art without a frame. It was photographed by Enrico Fontolan on February 2, 2019, and is available in color.

The painting "Copy after Portrait of Pope Leo X. with Cardinals Giuliano de'Medici and Luigi de'Rossi" is by the Florentine painter Giuliano di Piero di Simone Bugiardini. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 157 x 117.5 cm. The work was donated to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome in 1982 by the Torlonia family. It was previously in the private collection of the Torlonia family in Rome.

The copy after Raphael's painting depicts Pope Leo X. together with Cardinals Giuliano de'Medici and Luigi de'Rossi. An inscription on the front of the painting states that it was made by Giuliano Bugiardini after Raphael's original and commissioned by Cardinal Innocenzo Cybo, whose bearded head is depicted in the painting. Further information about the genesis and the work can be found in Vasari's biography of Giuliano Bugiardini and in the publication "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by Onori and Vodret.

The custodian of the object is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The object is held there under the number F.N. 584 and entered the gallery's collection in 1982 as a gift from the Torlonia family. Prior to that, the object was part of a private collection of the Torlonia family in Rome.

A digital photograph, part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana collection, is filed in the archive under the designation bhim00038787.tif. The photograph was digitized on April 24, 2019, and depicts the artwork "art 2019.04.24". Photographer Enrico Fontolan created the photograph in February 2019 as part of photography campaign 117/2019. The reverse side of the photograph has been released.

The painting "Copy after Portrait of Pope Leo X. with the Cardinals Giuliano de'Medici and Luigi de'Rossi" is by Giuliano Bugiardini and was donated to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome in 1982 by the Torlonia family. The work is a copy after the famous painting by Raphael and depicts Pope Leo X. together with the Cardinals Giuliano de'Medici and Luigi de'Rossi. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 157 x 117.5 cm. 

On the back of the painting is an inscription that reads: "Copiato dall'originale di Raffaele per mano di Giuliano Bugiardini / Per comando del Card: Innocenzo Cybo, di cui è ritratto / la Testa con la Barba". Vasari mentions the work in his second volume, third part, in the biography of Giuliano Bugiardini. The painting was previously in the private collection of the Torlonia family in Rome.

The custodian of the object is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The object was acquired in 1982 as a gift from the Torlonia family. It was previously in the private collection of the Torlonia family in Rome.

A photograph held at the Central Collecting Point Munich under the number CP132131 may depict a work by Johannes Felbermeyer from his estate (entered 1997). The photograph measures 16.4 x 12 cm and shows an overall view that has been released. 

Raro-Art dates the photograph to April 19, 2024.

The painting "The Hay Harvest" is by the Flemish master Pieter Bruegel the Elder and was created in 1565. The work, an oil painting on wood, measures 117 x 161 cm and is part of the collection of the Palais Lobkowitz Palace in Prague. It was previously in the private collection of Prince Lobkowitz and then in the Raudnitz collection on the Elbe.

Pieter Bruegel the Elder, known for his detailed and lively depictions of everyday life, has recreated the scene of the hay harvest in this painting with rich colors and impressive detail.
The object was previously owned by Raudnitz an der Elbe and subsequently came into the private collection of Prince Lobkowitz.

This image features a digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00002135. The photograph was added to the system on November 28, 2008, and is in color. The photograph was taken on July 14, 2005.

The panel painting "Death of Mary" is located in Rome, in the church of Santa Maria Maggiore, in the Chapter House. The painting was created between 73 and 74 AD and is part of the Hertziana Library in Rome.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from 1885 is depicted in this albumen print. The photograph was in the artist's possession and was made before 1957. The print is fully mounted and shows slight foxing. There are traces of insect damage on the right edge, which is also torn. The back has multiple inscriptions in ballpoint pen. The photograph is unstamped.

The organ wing with the Annunciation is from Conegliano and was created by Cima da Conegliano, also known as Giovanni Battista Cima. It is in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice. The organ wing is a panel painting and was cataloged in 1955 by Moschini Marconi (Cat. No. 120). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns two other paintings by Cima da Conegliano from this period: "Annunciation Angel" and "Mary of the Annunciation".

The painting "Annunciation Angel" measures 177 x 71 cm and has the inventory number 11 G 18 4. "Mary of the Annunciation" has the dimensions 172 x 78 cm and the inventory number 73 A 52 2. Both paintings are part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator for the Venice Galleria dell'Accademia is the office with numbers 398, 359, and 389.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from 1886 is preserved in this albumen print. The photograph comes from an album created before 1957. The print is fully adhered, with the lower right corner slightly bent. There are also traces of fingerprints and adhesive residue. The image shows slight fading. On the back, the letter "Vs." is written in ballpoint pen. There is no stamp and the photograph is released.

The organ wing with the Annunciation is from Conegliano and is located in the San Francesco Church in Conegliano. The administrator of the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice is responsible for the work. It was created by Cima da Conegliano, also known as Giovanni Battista Maler, Giovanni Battista Cima da Conegliano, Coneglianensis, Joannes Baptista Cima or Giambattista Giovanni Battista da Conegliano. The work is a panel painting and was exhibited in 1955 at the Moschini Marconi exhibition, Cat. No. 120, at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The organ wing is 177 cm high and 71 cm wide.

The organ wing comprises two paintings: Annunciation Angel and Mary of the Annunciation. The Annunciation Angel painting is 177 cm high and 71 cm wide. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome (epr,T,001). The Mary of the Annunciation painting is 172 cm high and 78 cm wide and is also located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome (epr,T,002).
The curator of the Venice Galleria dell'Accademia can be found in numbers 398, 359, and 389.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, designated "bhim00038780.tif", was taken on April 24, 2019. The photograph depicts the artwork "art" in color and was created by Enrico Fontolan as part of photography campaign 117/2019. The photograph shows the complete artwork with its frame.

The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini, published the Torlonia family's donation in 1892. The painting was previously in the private collection of the Valenti Gonzaga family in Rome. The publication of the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (2008) mentions the work on page 329. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the painting.

The curator of the collection is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini 817 (F.N. 1184). The collection was donated in 1892 by the Torlonia family. Previously, the collection was in private possession of the Valenti Gonzaga family in Rome.

The painting "Rocca Sinibalda" was painted in 1601 by Paul Bril and is part of a series depicting the estate of the Mattei family in Rocca Sinibalda. The work is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome and came into the museum's possession in 1939 through purchase from the private Mattei collection. The painting "Saint Jerome, Augustine, Peter, and Paul" is from Camerino and was painted by Carlo Crivelli before 1799. It is now in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice. The panel painting, which dates from around 1490, is part of a cycle that probably forms the sides of the "Madonna della candeletta", which is now in the Brera in Rome. The paintings "Saint Jerome", "Saint Augustine", "Saint Peter", and "Saint Paul" are fragmentary and are in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator for Venice is the Galleria dell'Accademia, located at 698.

The painting "The Brothers Bring Jacob Joseph's Bloodstained Cloak" is an oil painting on canvas measuring 170 x 200 cm. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (eds.), Rome 2008, page 172.
The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, acquired the object in 1694. The purchase was made by F.N. and confirmed in 1917 by G. Palumbo.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini acquired the painting "Saint Agnes Refuses to Worship the Pagan Gods" in 1971. The work is part of the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" published by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (Rome 2008, p. 118). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the painting.

The object custodian is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini 2538 (F.N. N/T). The object was acquired in 1971 as part of the Barberini Collection in Rome. Prior to that, the object was in the private collection of Francesco, Junior Barberini.

The painting "Portrait of a Lady" was probably created around 1555/1565 and is attributed to the Florentine painter Alessandro Allori. It was previously attributed to the painter Agnolo Bronzino. In 1512, the administrator of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi, Alessandro Allori, published a painting. The work, "Reclining Venus and Cupid," is an oil painting on canvas measuring 29 x 38.5 cm. The Expulsion from Paradise, a panel painting, was created by Marco Benefial. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 142 x 133 cm. Il XIX secolo" edited by E. di Majo and M. Lafranconi in 2006.

The authenticity of the painting was confirmed by F. Ferrari and G. Scavizzi, who documented it in their work "Luca Giordano - L'opera completa, Vol. 1" from 1992, catalogue A310. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also possesses further documentation of the work.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome published the painting "A Girl Among Plants" in 1887. The work entered the gallery in 1892 by donation. The former owner is unknown. The Gemäldegalerie in the Berlin Palace of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage acquired the painting around 1821. It is a panel painting on poplar wood with a diameter of 84 cm. The painting depicts Mary with the Child and two angels playing music. The Gemäldegalerie in the Berlin Palace of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage included the work in its general catalog in 1996, illustrated under number 1959.

The administrator of the Gemäldegalerie in the Berlin State Museum in Berlin-Dahlem is the Prussian Cultural Heritage. The painting was in private collections in London and Berlin before it was acquired by the Solly Collection in 1821. Edward Solly was the last owner before the painting entered the collection of the Prussian Cultural Heritage.
A photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, U.Pl. C 605_1-r, depicts a work of art from before 1940. The photograph is in black and white and has been released.

The painting "The Adoration of the Christ Child by the Shepherds" was published in 1908 by the administrator of the Museo Regionale di Messina. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 314 x 211 cm. The painting is attributed to Caravaggio, Michelangelo Merisi. Other spellings of the artist are Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, Merisi, Michelangelo Maresi, Michelangelo Marigi, Michelangelo Merighi, Michelangelo Merigi, Michelangelo Merizi, Michelangelo Morigi, Michelangelo Caraca da Caravaggio, Michelangelo Caravaggio, Michelangelo Merisi da Amerigi, Michelangelo Amerighi, Michelangelo Amarigi, Michelangelo Amorigi, Michelangelo Caravaggio, il Michelangelo Merisi Caravaggio. The painting is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Messina Regional Museum of Messina is Messina. The museum was founded in 1908.

The Holy Nicholas of Myra between two Deacons and Angels was painted in 1488 by Tommaso de Vigilia. The painting, executed on wood in oil, is a panel painting measuring 175 x 133 cm. The work is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was mentioned in the 1974 publication "M. C. Di Natale, Tommaso De Vigilia, Palermo".

The painting is part of the Galleria Colonna in Rome and is listed in the catalog "Galleria Colonna in Roma: Catalogo dei dipinti" by P. Piergiovanni (ed.) from 2015 under catalog number 2. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the work.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Colonna was Girolamo Colonna, a cardinal who lived before 1642. He resided in the Sala Grande.

The public collection of the Huntington Library, Art Gallery and Botanical Gardens in California houses the painting "The Blue Boy" by Thomas Gainsborough. The Huntington Library, Art Gallery and Botanical Gardens is managed by the public agency, Verwalter San Marino (California).

The hermit triptych "Saint Anthony, Saint Jerome, and Saint Aegidius" was created by Hieronymus Bosch around 1505. The triptych consists of three panel paintings that use oil on wood as a ground. The three paintings each depict a saint: Anthony, Jerome, and Aegidius. The triptych is located in the Sala dei Tre Capi in the Palazzo Ducale in Venice. It was mentioned by U. Franzoi in his 1982 publication "History and Legend of the Doge's Palace of Venice".

The paintings are documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The dimensions of the paintings are: "Saint Anthony" 29.5 x 85 cm, "Saint Jerome" 60 x 85 cm, and "Saint Aegidius" 86.5 x 29 cm.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the identification number bhim00017275. The photograph is part of the "art" collection and was digitized on November 29, 2016. It is in color and depicts a work by the artist Roberto Sigismondi. The rights to the image are divided and released for use.

The Galleria Colonna in Rome houses a painting by Francesco Albani, created around 1640/1642. The work, a variation of the famous Abduction of Europe, was restored in 2002 and is in the possession of the National Gallery in London. The painter Francesco Albani was born around 1578 and worked in Rome. 

The Galleria Colonna in Rome may have been under the direction of Girolamo Colonna, a cardinal, at one time. The former owner of the painting was Francesco Albani.

The administrator of the Galleria Colonna, Girolamo Colonna (Cardinal), had the Sala dell'Apoteosi di Martino V. created around 1642. The painting "Fall of the Damned" by Hieronymus Bosch is located in the Doge's Palace in Venice. It was created between 1500 and 1504 and belongs to a cycle of four depictions of the afterlife. The oil paintings on wood were published by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. 

The painting is part of a cycle of four paintings in total, which deal with the themes "Fall of the Damned", "Hell", "Ascent of the Saved into Paradise" and "Heavenly Paradise". All four paintings measure 88.5 x 41.5 cm and are oil on wood.

The painting "The Canal Grande with the Rialto Bridge from the South" was created by Giovanni Antonio Canaletto, also known as Canaletto, around the year 1697. The oil painting on canvas depicts a view of the Rialto Bridge in Venice and the Canal Grande from the south. The work is part of the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome.

The dimensions of the painting are 68.5 x 92 cm. It is listed under the inventory numbers 25 I 14 51 and 25 I 12 61.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is Palazzo Barberini 1033.

The painting "Venus' Toilet" was created by Francesco Albani in 1578. The circular canvas painting, with a diameter of 154 cm, depicts the scene of Venus bathing. The custodian of the painting "Christ Served by Angels" has been the Museo del Prado in Madrid since 1967. Prior to that, it was part of the Handel Hallsborough Gallery in London until 1967. The painting was created around 1705 by Alessandro Magnasco. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 193 x 142.2 cm. The work depicts a landscape with Christ and angels after the temptation.

The object's administrator has been the Museo del Prado in Madrid since 1967. Prior to the Museo del Prado assuming responsibility, the Handel Hallsborough Gallery in London was the object's administrator until 1967.

The Holy Crispinus is the subject of a panel painting attributed to the painter Domenico Corvi. A digital photograph, part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the image identification bhim00037057.tif and bhim00037057 mus 2018.10.17 HER0166.tif. The photograph is in color and shows a full view of the artwork with its frame. It was taken by Enrico Fontolan in August 2018 and released.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini published a ceiling painting attributed to Andrea Sacchi. The painting, depicting the Allegory of Divine Wisdom, was created around 1658 and is a copy of Sacchi's work. The oil painting on canvas measures 160 x 200 cm and is located in the Sala della Divina Sapienza in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome.

The work was mentioned in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" edited by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (2008).
The administrator of the property is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. The property is located at Palazzo Barberini, address 4567.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from the period 1940 to 1944 is in an albumen print. The photograph is fully mounted and faded. Two small photographs are glued together on the back, and a stamp is present. 

The photograph is restricted.

The painting "Footwashing" was made by Giovanni Agostino da Lodi, also known as Pseudo-Boccaccino, around the year 1500 in Venice. The work is a panel painting on wood and measures 131 x 111 cm. The curators of the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice hold the painting in their collection.

The dating of the painting to the year 1500 is confirmed by Moschini and Marconi from 1955, catalogue number 189. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the painting.
Responsibility for the property lies with the manager Venice. The manager's contact details are: Gallerie dell'Accademia 90.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the ID bhim00039589.tif depicts a detail of "The Arrest of Christ". The photograph was taken on May 26, 2022, and is in color. It is part of a photo campaign by Roberto Sigismondi from 2019. Use of the photograph has been authorized.

In the Palazzo della Valle in Rome, on the first floor, is the Sala delle Sibille. The coffered ceiling of this room is decorated with depictions of Sibylls and was probably made by Francesco Salviati or his workshop. The ceiling, made of painted wood, dates from the period between 1523 and 1550. The ceiling was painted in several parts, including the Cumean Sibyl, the Erythraean Sibyl, the Persian Sibyl, and the European Sibyl.

The paintings of the Sibylls were documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and are part of the collection "Rom 2022.05.30,T,001" to "Rom 2022.05.30,T,004". L. Grieco examined the ceiling in detail in his work "Opus incertum" published in 2017.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the signature bhim00039597.tif and the number bhim00039597, was taken on May 30, 2022. The photograph is in color and shows a detail of "The Adoration of the Magi" by Roberto Sigismondi from the photo campaign 12/2019. Use of the image has been authorized.

In Rome, in the Palazzo della Valle, on the first floor, in the Sala delle Sibille, there is a coffered ceiling with depictions of the Sibyls. The ceiling is attributed to Francesco Salviati and dates from between 1523 and 1550. It is made of painted wood. L. Grieco examines the ceiling in his work "Il soffitto delle Sibille nel palazzo del cardinale Della Valla a Roma," which appeared in the publication "Opus incertum."

The ceiling depicts four Sibyl figures: the Cumaean Sibyl, the Erythraean Sibyl, the Persian Sibyl, and the European Sibyl. The paintings are part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00039598.tif, depicts a detail of the Annunciation of the Birth of Christ to the Shepherds. The photograph, taken in color on May 30, 2022, is part of Roberto Sigismondi's 2019 photographic campaign. It has been released for use. 

The framing of the detail is also visible in the photograph.

In Rome, in the Palazzo della Valle, on the noble floor, is the Sala delle Sibille. The coffered ceiling of this room is adorned with depictions of the Sibylls and is attributed to Francesco Salviati. The ceiling painting dates from the period between 1523 and 1550. The ceiling, made of painted wood, is part of a larger collection of paintings housed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The Bibliotheca Hertziana documents the individual Sibylline depictions on the ceiling. Among the depicted Sibylls are the Cumean Sibyl, the Erythraean Sibyl, the Persian Sibyl, and the European Sibyl.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00039600.tif, depicts a detail of the Flagellation of Christ. The photograph was taken on May 30, 2022, by Roberto Sigismondi as part of a 2019 photography campaign. The frame of the image is in focus. The photograph is in color and has been released.

In the Palazzo della Valle in Rome, on the first floor, in the Sala delle Sibille, there is a coffered ceiling with Sibyl depictions dating from 1523/1550. The ceiling is attributed to the painter Francesco Salviati, possibly also Cecchino Rossi or Francesco de' Francesco Salviati. The painted wooden ceiling shows various Sibyls, including the Cumaean, the Erythraean, the Persian, and the European Sibyl.

The individual paintings of the Sibyls have been documented and published by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A photograph from Marburg, taken on April 3, 2000, shows a family chapel. The black-and-white photograph is from a KHI photo campaign in 2000 that focused on family chapels. The shot is part of a series that documented a total of 200 family chapels.

The overall view of the chapel is blocked.

The altar, located to the left of the main altar in the Santa Maria in Gradi church in Arezzo, was made by Bernardino di Bartolommeo Santini. The painting, created in 1629, depicts the Crucifixion of Christ with the Saints Bruno of Querfurt and Andrew. It is an oil painting on canvas.

The scene is divided into three parts. On the left is the painting "Saint Bruno of Querfurt Passes the Fire Test," and on the right is the "Miracle of Nicaea of Saint Andrew." The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds three publications on this altar: T,001 shows the entire Crucifixion scene, T,002 focuses on Bruno of Querfurt, and T,003 on the Miracle of Nicaea of Saint Andrew. Further information can be found in the "Guida storico-artistica" by A. Tafi (1978) and in "Bernardino Santini pittore in Arezzo" by L. Fornasari (2000).

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi from 1298-88, designated "bhex-si-2019-01-461", was colorized on June 11, 2020. The photograph shows a full view and was acquired by Roberto Sigismondi in 2017. The order was placed between 01-05/2019. The usage rights are divided.

The oil painting "The Holy Martyrs Rufinus and Vittorino Receive the Crown of Martyrdom" was created in 1657 in Assisi by the painter Giacomo Giorgetti, attributed to. The canvas painting is in the possession of the Pinacoteca Comunale in Assisi and is part of the Palazzo Vallemani. 

The work, measuring 135 x 136 cm, depicts the Saints Rufinus and Vittorino of Assisi receiving the crown of martyrdom. 
The painting was created in the attic of the town hall in Assisi.
The manager of the Assisi Pinacoteca Comunale is the Palazzo Vallemani firm, located at 83, 87.

An unknown photograph from the rare items department dates from the period between 1940 and 1944. It is an albumen print, completely mounted and heavily faded. On the back are two cardboard mounts glued together, and a stamp.

The painting "The Bearded Woman" (Maddalena Ventura with her husband) dates from 1631 and is the work of the Spanish painter Jusepe de Ribera. It was published in the Museo de la Fundación Duque de Lerma, Hospital Tavera in Toledo. The painting is an oil painting on canvas and depicts a woman with a beard, together with her husband. The dimensions of the painting are 196 x 127 cm.

The image description was documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome under the catalogue number 42 D 3 61 BB 2 (VENTURA, Maddalena).

The oil painting on canvas measures 73 cm in height and 36 cm in width. It is in the private collection of a manager from Naples and was previously part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. 

The work is a panel painting and an example of 17th-century Italian painting.

The painting "The Apostles Peter and Paul Embrace Shortly Before Their Execution" is from the workshop of the Italian painter Giovanni Serodine and dates from around 1620/1625. The oil painting on canvas measures 144 x 220 cm and is part of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome. 

The work was acquired by the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in 1968 and has been in its possession ever since. The original provenance of the painting is Rome, where it was kept in the Palazzo Mattei di Giove.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome is the Palazzo Barberini. It was appointed administrator in 1968.

The Hermit Onuphrius by Giovanni Battista Caracciolo is an oil painting on canvas depicting Saint Onuphrius. The painting was published in 1535 by the administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini. It measures 180.5 cm in height and 116.6 cm in width.  

The work is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was described by Onori and Vodret in their catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" published in 2008.

The triptych "Scenes from the Passion of Christ" originates from Altomonte and was painted around 1401/1410 by the Master of Antonio and Onofrio Penna. The panel painting, which is located in the Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione in Altomonte, is a work of the Italian Renaissance. The triptych consists of three parts and depicts scenes from the Passion of Jesus Christ. The individual parts are: "The Kiss of Judas," "Christ before Anna," "Christ before the High Council," "Christ before Pontius Pilate," "Christ before Herod," "Christ before Pontius Pilate," "Christ is scourged by soldiers," "Crowning of Thorns," "Carrying of the Cross," "Crucifixion of Christ," "Lamentation of Christ," and "Resurrection of Christ." 

The individual parts of the triptych are in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager is the Altomonte Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione.
A scan of the image "Sopr. BAS BO GFS_153744.tif" has been made. It is a bhex-sopr-bas-bo-gfs artwork, dated April 23, 2007. The image is in color (Ektachrome) and is restricted.

The Crucifixion of Christ was painted by Prospero Fontana, the curator of the Bolognese Museo di San Giuseppe. The painting, an oil on canvas panel, measures 73 cm in height by 64 cm in width. It is now housed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The painting "Saint Jerome" was made around 1570 by Jacopo Bassano, Giacomo Bassano, or Jacopo dal Ponte from Bassano. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 119 x 154 cm. The work is in the possession of the manager of the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice.

The manager of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi is Florence. The object was created in 1468 and has the number P 1416.

The painting "Saint Catherine of Alexandria" was created in 1601/1650 by an unknown artist. The convent church Chiesa di Badia Sante Flora e Lucilla in Arezzo houses a sculpture of Saints Flora and Lucilla. The sculpture was made by Girolamo Particini in 1651 and is made of wood and gilded with gold. It is located on the organ loft and consists of relief sculpture and round sculpture. Raffaello Vanni painted the paintings of Saints Flora and Lucilla. The paintings were also painted in 1651 on canvas with oil and are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The paintings of Saints Flora and Lucilla were mentioned in the "Guida storica-artistica" by A. Tafi from 1978 in Arezzo.

In Rome, in the Santa Maria della Pace, the Cappella del Crocifisso chapel is located in the octagon, in the third chapel to the left. The painting there is by Jacopo Zucchi and was created between 1551 and 1600. The painting depicts Saints Martha and Mary Magdalene. It is rectangular and oil on canvas.

The painting is part of a series of paintings that serve as a pendant to a work by Ventura Salimbeni. Information about the work can be found in the publication "Roma Sacra. Guida alle chiese della città eterna, Itinerario 11, Naples/Rome 1997" by Maria Pia D'Orazio. Further details were researched at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome in 2021 and confirmed in May 2023.

The painting was probably created between 1630 and 1650 and depicts the Resurrection of Christ. It is an oil painting on canvas, measuring 73 cm x 16 cm.

The work was described by P. Palazzotto in his publication "Palermo: guida agli oratori" from 2004 and in "Giacomo Serpotta: gli oratori di Palermo, guida storico-artistica" from 2016. Further information can be found at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata in Sant'Agata de' Goti houses a fresco depicting the Last Judgment, dating from around 1404/1414. The frescoes were restored between 1973 and 1977. The painting, executed in tempera on plaster, is divided into three registers.

In the upper register, Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist are depicted. In the middle register, on the left, the resurrection of the dead is shown, and on the right, purgatory. In the lower register, on the left, is heavenly Jerusalem, and on the right, hell.
A black and white photograph shows Max Hutzel at his campsite in 1964. The photograph is a detail and some areas are obscured.

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built and restored between 1404/1414 and 1973/1977. The wall painting "Last Judgment" is a striking example of the art of that time. The painting was executed in tempera on plaster.

The Last Judgment is divided into three registers. The upper register shows Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist. The middle register, on the left, depicts the Resurrection of the Dead, and on the right, Purgatory. The lower register shows, on the left, heavenly Jerusalem and, on the right, Hell.

The Chiesa Madre Santa Maria Assunta church in Petralia Sottana houses a panel painting from the period 1586/1615. It depicts the Madonna dell'Itria or Odigitria. The panel painting "Madonna Appears to Saint Anthony of Padua" is located in the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti. The painting, which was executed on canvas in oil, is probably from the period between 1651 and 1750. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns the artwork.

The panel painting "Annunciation" dates from between 1870 and 1887 and was made by Giuseppe Maler in Cosenza. The oil painting on canvas is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The original location of the work was the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti.

The publication of the painting can be found in the work "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (eds.), Rome 2008, page 462. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the painting.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, acquired the painting "Flight into Egypt" in 1895 by purchase from the Monte di Pietà. The work, an oil painting on copper, was created by Domenichino, possibly also by Zampieri, Domenico Giampieri, or Domenico. The painting measures 41.5 x 31.5 cm and is part of the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini.

Vodret (eds.), published in 2008 in Rome, on page 465. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also holds information about the painting.

The custodian of the object is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The object was acquired in 1895 by purchase from the Monte di Pietà. The object's inventory number is F.N. 1040.

The painting "Beheading of John the Baptist" is an oil painting on canvas measuring 133 x 96.5 cm. It comes from the workshop of the Dutch painter Gerrit van Honthorst and was copied by Gherardo della Notte. The work was donated to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome in 1892 by the Torlonia Collection. Previously, it was in a private collection in Rome, Villa Albani.

The curator of the collection is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The collection was acquired in 1892 by gift (Torlonia) and was previously in a private collection in Rome, the Villa Albani.

The painting "Still Life with Flowers and Fruit" was created by Luca Forte around 1630-1640. The oil painting on canvas measures 77 x 101 cm. It is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini and was published in Rome by the curator in 1930. The work is part of an extensive bibliographical research project dealing with Italian still life painting.

The painting is analyzed and discussed in various publications, including "Civiltà del Seicento a Napoli" by Bellucci E., "La natura morta italiana" by Salerno L., "La natura morta in Italia" by Porzio F. and Zeri F., and "La natura morta al tempo di Caravaggio" by Cottino A. The Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom holds further information and documents relating to the work.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is the Palazzo Barberini, built in 1930.

The oil painting "Saint Martyr" created in 1626/1650 comes from the workshop of the Italian painter Massimo Stanzione. The painting, which uses oil on canvas, is today in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. It depicts the Saint Martyr and was created in Naples, in the church of San Giorgio a Cremano.

The design for an allegory of Fortitudo with Fides and Caritas is by Giovanni Battista Gaulli, also known as il Bacciccia. The painting, an oil painting on canvas, was acquired in 1668 by the administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Palazzo Barberini. It depicts the three virtues Fortitudo, Fides, and Caritas and measures 60 x 50 cm. The work was acquired by Palumbo in 1916 and is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome.

Further information about the painting can be found in the publication "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" edited by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (Rome 2008, p. 209). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also holds further information about this work.
The custodian of the object is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini from 1668. The object was acquired in 1916 by purchase (Palumbo).

The design for Allegory of Fortitude with Fides and Caritas is a panel painting created in 1668 by Giovanni Battista Gaulli, also known as il Bacciccia. The work is currently in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome and entered the collection in 1916 by purchase (Palumbo).

The oil painting on canvas measures 60 x 50 cm and was described in the literature by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" from 2008.

The object is in the possession of the manager of the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini. It was acquired in 1668 by F.N. and came into the possession of the gallery in 1916 through purchase (Palumbo).

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini acquired the painting "Cyrus, King of Persia" in 1962. It is part of the presbytery and is situated above the high altar. The painting, attributed to Antonio Grano, was painted on canvas between 1701 and 1710. It depicts the King of the Visigoths finding Saint Aegidius in his forest hermitage. The oil painting is in the Hertziana Library in Rome.

The painting "Bacchus and Ariadne" was painted by the Roman artist Francesco Romanelli around 1660. It is owned by the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome and was acquired there in 1971. The oil painting on canvas measures 127 x 267 cm and has the inventory numbers 92L1781 and 92L1212.  

Art historical research on the work has been advanced by the publication of the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in 2008. A detailed description of the painting can be found on page 336 of this catalog.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is Palazzo Barberini 2531 (F.N. N/T). The object was acquired in 1971.

The painter Giacomo Ceruti, also known as Pitocchetto, created the portrait of an unknown man smoking a pipe around 1730-1735. The painting, an oil on canvas panel painting, depicts the man in three-quarter profile and measures 213.5 x 142 cm. 

The work is in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. It was acquired by the Roman institution in 1941 and was previously part of the private Martinengo collection in Brescia until 1939. A detailed description of the painting can be found in the publication "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (2008).

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini acquired the object in 1987 (F.N.) by purchase. Prior to that, the object was in a private collection in Brescia, the Martinengo Collection, until 1939.

The Madonna with Musical Angels originates from Naples and was created in 1688. The oil painting on canvas depicts the scene in a chapel in Castel Nuovo Castle. The chapel is named Cappella di San Francesco di Paola. Unfortunately, the artwork was destroyed by a bomb hit in 1943.

The Hertziana Library in Rome still possesses fragments of the painting, documented under the designations 11 F 5 (+3) 11 G 21.

The painting "Madonna with Musical Angels" was created around 1688 in Naples in the Castel Nuovo castle, in the chapel of the Cappella di San Francesco di Paola. The painting, an oil painting on canvas, was destroyed in 1943 by a bomb hit. 

The picture was in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome before its destruction.

The painting "Annunciation" was created around 1688 by Nicolo Russo. It is located in the Museo Civico in Castel Nuovo in Naples. The work is an oil painting on canvas and measures 73 A x 52.3 cm. The chapel Cappella di San Francesco di Paola in Castel Nuovo also houses a work by the artist, which is on display there. Nicolo Russo was a painter from Naples and may have also worked with other artists such as Painter Rossi and Nicolo Rosso.
The administrator of the Naples Museo Civico in Castel Nuovo is the Naples Museo Civico.

The panel painting "Saint Francis" originates from Montepulciano and was created between 1301 and 1350. The tempera painting on wood is 11 H high and is kept in the Museo Civico Pinacoteca Crociani in Siena.  

The anonymous artist painted the work for the church of San Francesco in Montepulciano. The church had commissioned the administrator of the Museo Civico in Montepulciano to manage the painting. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has mentioned the work in its collection.
The property manager is the Montepulciano Museo Civico with property number 71/128.

The painter Raphael, also known as Raffaello Sanzio, Raffaello Sanzio, Raffaele Raffaello Santi, Raphael Urbinas, Raphaello or Raphael, created the painting "Portrait of Cesare Borgia". The "Throned Madonna and Saints" (Madonna del Baldacchino) is a wooden panel painting created between 1506 and 1508 by Raphael. The painting is in the care of the Gallerie degli Uffizi and the Galleria Palatina in the Palazzo Pitti in Florence. Raphael, the artist, was also known as Raphael Santi, Raffaele, Raffaello Sanzio, Raffaello, Raphael Urbinas, Raphaello, and Raphael.

Originally, the work was placed in the Augustiner Santo Spirito monastery church in Florence in the Cappella Dei chapel. Later, it was moved to the Domkapelle Cappella dei Turini in Pescia (Pistoia).
The manager of the Uffizi Gallery is the Palatine Gallery in the Pitti Palace in Florence.

The altarpiece "Angels Adoring the Image of Grace of the Madonna della Vallicella" was created in 1608 in Rome in the workshop of the Flemish painter Peter Paul Rubens. The painting, which is part of the collection "T,001", depicts angels adoring the Image of Grace of the Madonna della Vallicella. It is located in the church of Santa Maria in Vallicella in Rome, more precisely in the apse, to the right of the high altar. The painting was executed on slate and measures 420 x 255 cm.

It is a pendant to the paintings "The Holy Saints Gregory the Great, Papianus and Maurus" and "The Holy Saints Domitilla, Nereus and Achilleus" by Rubens. The Holy Saints Domitilla, Nereus and Achilleus are each 11 HH high. The work was documented in the "Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom" by C. Barbieri, S. Barchiesi and D. Ferrara in 1995.
